IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p155/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p155/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p155/r4.claim: He treats the bāʾ in باسم as extra, giving the meaning ‘read the name of your Lord’.

MAJAZ:v1p14/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p14/r10.claim: He groups these as two wordings where a governing particle is expressed in one place and omitted in the other.
MAJAZ:v1p14/r10.anchor: قال: «وإذا قرأت القرآن» (16/ 98) وقال: «اقرأ باسم ربك» (96/ 1) .

BURHAN:v1p206/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.speaker: عائشة
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.claim: The beginning-of-revelation report in al-Bukhari, explicitly authenticated by al-Hakim from Aisha, establishes اقرأ as the first revelation; Muslim gives it through “He taught man what he did not know.”
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.anchor: وأخرجه الحاكم فى مستدركه من حديث عائشة رضى الله عنها صريحا وقال صحيح الإسناد

BURHAN:v1p206/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p206/r2.claim: Muslim’s wording extends the first revelation through “He taught man what he did not know”; al-Bukhari’s version stops at “your Lord is most generous,” which the author calls an accepted abridgment.
BURHAN:v1p206/r2.anchor: ولفظ مسلم أول ما نزل من القرآن

BURHAN:v1p206/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p206/r6.claim: Taken together, the reports show that اقرأ was the first revelation absolutely and al-Muddaththir followed it after the pause.
BURHAN:v1p206/r6.anchor: فقد أخبر فى هذا الحديث عن الملك الذى جاءه بحراء قبل هذه المرة

BURHAN:v1p206/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r7.speaker: ابن حيان
BURHAN:v1p206/r7.claim: Ibn Hibban likewise sees no conflict: اقرأ came at Hira, then after the Prophet returned to Khadija, al-Muddaththir was revealed in her house.
BURHAN:v1p206/r7.anchor: وكذلك قال ابن حيان فى صحيحه لا تضاد بين الحديثين

ITQAN:v1p75/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.claim: Ubayd b. ʿUmayr says Gabriel brought the Prophet a silk sheet and told him to recite; he identifies the opening of al-ʿAlaq as the first sura sent down.
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أشتة في كتاب المصاحف عن عبيد بن عمير قال جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بنمط فقال اقرأ

ITQAN:v1p75/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.speaker: الزهري
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī recounts that while the Prophet was at Ḥirāʾ, an angel brought a silk sheet inscribed with the opening verses of al-ʿAlaq.
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.anchor: وأخرج عن الزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذ أتى ملك بنمط من ديباج فيه مكتوب

ITQAN:v1p75/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p75/r4.claim: One reconciliation distinguishes the first complete sura, al-Muddaththir, from the first verses revealed, the beginning of al-ʿAlaq.
ITQAN:v1p75/r4.anchor: أحدها أن السؤال كان عن نزول سورة كاملة فبين أن سورة المدثر نزلت بكمالها قبل نزول تمام سورة اقرأ

ITQAN:v1p75/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p75/r5.claim: A second authentic report places al-Muddaththir after the pause in revelation: the Prophet saw the same angel previously encountered at Ḥirāʾ, showing the Ḥirāʾ revelation came earlier.
ITQAN:v1p75/r5.anchor: ويؤيد هذا ما في الصحيحين أيضا عن أبي سلمة عن جابر سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يحدث عن فترة الوحي

ITQAN:v1p75/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p75/r7.claim: The final reconciliation says al-ʿAlaq was first for prophethood, while al-Muddaththir was first for the mission and command to warn.
ITQAN:v1p75/r7.anchor: ثالثها أن المراد أولية مخصوصة بالأمر بالإنذار وعبر بعضهم عن هذا بقوله أول ما نزل للنبوة ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r1.claim: There is no contradiction: Jabir heard only the later revelation episode, not its beginning, so he supposed al-Muddaththir was first; it was first after Iqra.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r1.anchor: وذلك أن جابرا سمع من النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - هذه القصة الأخيرة ولم يسمع أولها فتوهم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r3.claim: The report shows that revelation paused after Iqra and then resumed with يا أيها المدثر; the Hira angel episode therefore occurred after Iqra.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r3.anchor: وبان بهذا الحديث أن الوحي كان قد فتر بعد نزول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r1.claim: The surah commands worship of the Creator, especially for the person favored in the prior surah, as gratitude, avoidance of ingratitude, hope for Paradise, and fear of Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r1.anchor: مقصودها الأمر لا سيما للمقصود بالتفضيل في سورة التين بعبادة من له الخلق والأمر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r2.claim: Both names point to the command: the Lord who nurtures deserves thanks, while reading signals the command to worship and implies salvation at the final judgment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r2.anchor: لأن المربي يجب شكره ، ويحرم غاية التحريم كفره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r3.claim: The name al-ʿAlaq points to creation and return: whoever knows they were made from a clot can recognize God's power to recreate them from dust, which is more receptive to life.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r3.anchor: والعلق يدل على كل من النهاية ثم البداية بالالتزام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r5.claim: The basmala names God's perfection, universal mercy deserving gratitude, and special mercy through which chosen servants receive gifts.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r5.anchor: وفق من شاء من خواصه لما أنالهم به المواهب السنية

BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r1.claim: Calling God the Creator recalls the first blessing and proves that the One who gave humanity life and its perfections can teach reading; creation belongs solely to Him.
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r1.anchor: وصف الرب به لتذكير أول النعماء الفائضة عليه منه تعالى والتنبيه على أن من قدر على خلق الإنسان

BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r2.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r2.claim: Fath al-Rahman says the Creator attribute answers Arabs who called idols lords, since idols cannot share in creating.
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r2.anchor: وقال في فتح الرحمن لما ذكر الرب وكانت العرب في الجاهلية تسمى الأصنام أربابا

BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r3.claim: Iqra is a command, repeated to reinforce the obligation and introduce a new sentence about the most generous Lord; a permissible pause follows خلق because the Prophet had objected that he could not read.
BURSEVI:v10p363#3/r3.anchor: وكرر علامة الأمر بالقراءة تأكيدا للإيجاب وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من قوله تعالى

QASHANI:96:1-2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:1-2/r1.claim: This is the first rank of the Prophet’s return from unity to differentiation and is said to be the first revealed surah. The bāʾ marks instrumental aid: after returning from God to creation, he has gifted divine existence and qualities and is therefore a name, essence with attribute; he reads through the essential existence that is the greatest name.
QASHANI:96:1-2/r1.anchor: نزلت في أول رتبة رده عليه السلام عن الجمع إلى التفصيل

QASHANI:96:1-2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:1-2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:1-2/r2.claim: The Lord who created means that He manifested Himself under the form of creation: the Prophet appears in his own form, stands through God in created form, and returns from divine unity to creaturely differentiation.
QASHANI:96:1-2/r2.anchor: احتجب بصورة الخلق، يعني ظهرت بصورتك

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r1.claim: Hearing the basmala brings either sobriety, when heard through knowledge and clear proof, or effacement, when heard through direct recognition and bewilderment before God's dominion.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r1.anchor: إما صحوا لمن سمعها بشاهد العلم فيستبصر بواضح برهانه ، أو محوا لمن سمعها بشاهد المعرفة لأنه يتحير

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r2.claim: The opening verses were among the first revelations to the Chosen One, when Gabriel came to him in the air and commanded him to read.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r2.anchor: هذه السورة من أول ما نزل على المصطفى لما تعرض له جبريل في الهواء ، ونزل عليه فقال

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r3.claim: All other people are seekers, but Muhammad was the one sought and chosen.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r3.anchor: فالناس كلهم مريدون - وهو كان مرادا

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r4.claim: Muhammad answered twice that he was not a reader, then Gabriel instructed him to read as he was told.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r4.anchor: ما أنا بقارئ ، فقال له : اقرأ ، فقال : ما أنا بقارئ ، فقال له :

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r5.claim: “Who created” means that God created people as they are.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r5.anchor: أي خلقهم على ما هم به

SULAMI:v2p407/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p407/r1.claim: Seekers pursue God, while those sought by God are themselves sought; Abraham searched, but the beloved is sought, and the command to read came to Muhammad without prior seeking.
SULAMI:v2p407/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أهل الإرادة في الطلب ، والمرادون مطلوبون ألا ترى إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r1.claim: Aisha reports that the first Qur'anic surah revealed was named by its opening words, Iqra bi-smi rabbika; several Successors transmit the same title, used by al-Tirmidhi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r1.anchor: روي في ( المستدرك ) عن عائشة : ( أول سورة نزلت من القرآن اقرأ باسم ربك )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r2.claim: It is also commonly called al-Alaq because that word occurs near the beginning; Bukhari titles it Iqra bi-smi rabbika alladhi khalaq, and others call it Iqra or Iqra wa-l-Alaq.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r2.anchor: وسميت في المصاحف ومعظم التفاسير ( سورة العلق ) لوقوع لفظ ( العلق )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya and Ibn al-Arabi call this surah al-Qalam, while those who do so call the other surah Nun; al-Suyuti does not list this one among surahs with multiple names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r3.anchor: وعنونها ابن عطية وأبو بكر بن العربي : ( سورة القلم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r4.claim: The surah is Meccan by agreement and was the first revealed; its first five verses came in Hira during Ramadan on the seventeenth, year forty after the Elephant, according to sound Aisha reports and most exegetes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r4.anchor: وهي أول سورة نزلت في القرآن كما ثبت في الأحاديث الصحيحة الواضحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r5.speaker: جابر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r5.claim: Jabir says al-Muddaththir was first; Ibn Ashur reconciles this as the first revelation after the pause, like al-Duha after the second pause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r5.anchor: وعن جابر أول سورة المدثر ، وتؤول بأن كلامه نص أن سورة المدثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r6.claim: Verse-count traditions give twenty verses in Medina and Mecca, eighteen in Syria, and nineteen in Kufa and Basra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r6.anchor: وعدد آيها في عد أهل المدينة ومكة عشرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r7.claim: The surah teaches Muhammad to recite Qur'anic speech though he did not previously know recitation, and suggests that God can directly enable knowledge as He enabled writing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p433/r7.anchor: تلقين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الكلام القرآني وتلاوته إذ كان لا يعرف التلاوة من قبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p434#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p434#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p434#2/r1.claim: This is the first Qur'an revealed to Muhammad, as established in the forthcoming report from Aisha.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p434#2/r1.anchor: هذا أول ما أوحي به من القرآن إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p434#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p434#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p434#2/r2.claim: Opening with 'Recite' announces that the Messenger will become a reciter of scripture although he had not recited scripture before revelation; it is a fitting opening for the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p434#2/r2.anchor: وافتتاح السورة بكلمة { اقرأ } إيذان بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سيكون قارئا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r1.claim: Iqra literally commands reading aloud of specified written or memorized words; the grammatical discussion parallels the command in al-Nahl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { اقرأ } أمر بالقراءة ، والقراءة نطق بكلام معين مكتوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r2.claim: The imperative asks for immediate or near-future recitation of words about to be dictated, since no text had previously been read or handed to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r2.anchor: فالمطلوب بقوله : { اقرأ } أن يفعل القراءة في الحال أو المستقبل القريب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.claim: Aisha narrates in the two Sahihs that Gabriel came to Muhammad in Hira, commanded him three times, embraced him forcefully each time, then recited the opening through 'what he did not know.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.anchor: وفي حديث ( الصحيحين ) عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قولها فيه : ( حتى جاءه الحق وهو في غار حراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.claim: Aisha's narration is directly from the Prophet; her account that he returned trembling with the passage means he retained and recited what had been dictated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.anchor: فهذا الحديث روته عائشة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقولها قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.claim: Khadija's request that Waraqa hear him further indicates Muhammad recited the revealed passage immediately; Gabriel's repeated command repeated God's wording to accustom him to reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.anchor: وهذا ينبىء بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عندما قيل له بعد الفطة الثالثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r1.claim: Calling God 'the Creator' implies exclusive divinity: because He alone created, people should invoke Him rather than al-Lat or al-Uzza, though the polytheists acknowledged His creation of heaven and earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r1.anchor: وجيء في وصف الرب بطريق الموصول { الذي خلق } ولأن في ذلك استدلالا على انفراد الله بالإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r3.claim: The object after the first 'created' may be omitted because the verb is intransitive, to mean the Creator; omitted for generality, to mean all creation; or supplied by the next phrase as 'humanity.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r3.anchor: وعدم ذكر مفعول لفعل { خلق } يجوز أن يكون لتنزيل الفعل منزلة اللازم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r1.claim: The second command to recite repeats the first to give it additional emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r1.anchor: وفعل { اقرأ } الثاني تأكيد ل { اقرأ } الأول للاهتمام بهذا الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.claim: The opening five verses gather divine attributes: lordship implies existence and oneness, creation and teaching indicate acts, and al-Akram entails perfection and freedom from deficiency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآيات الخمس من أول السورة أصول الصفات الإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.claim: The initial command and reference to pen teaching imply that Muhammad remained unlettered, an attribute completing the Qur'an's miracle, as another verse states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.anchor: وفي الاقتصار على أمر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقراءة ثم إخباره بأن الله علم الإنسان بالقلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.claim: These are the final five verses of the passage first revealed at Hira; the following discussion on verses 6–10 begins a new subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.anchor: وهذه آخر الخمس الآيات التي هي أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r2.claim: Read in the name of your Lord means begin the action by mentioning God, as in the command to board the ship in God's name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r2.anchor: ومعنى هذه الآية، اقرأ هذا القرآن باسم ربك، أي ابدأ فعلك بذكر اسم ربك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r3.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r3.claim: Al-Tha'labi gives another interpretation: recite the basmala at the beginning of every surah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r3.anchor: ووجه آخر في كتاب الثعلبي أن المعنى: اقرأ في أول كل سورة، وقراءة بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r4.claim: A third interpretation takes the commanded reading itself to be the words “in the name of your Lord who created.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r4.anchor: ووجه آخر أن يكون المقروء الذي أمر بقراءته هو باسم ربك الذي خلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r5.claim: Because Arabs in the pre-Islamic period called idols lords, God is qualified as the Creator, a feature the idols cannot share.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r5.anchor: ولما ذكر الرب وكانت العرب في الجاهلية تسمي الأصنام أربابا جاءه بالصفة التي لا شركة للأصنام فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p174/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p174/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p174/r4.claim: Sura al-Alaq is also called Sura al-Qalam; it is Meccan by consensus and was the first revelation, with five verses revealed first and the remainder later concerning Abu Jahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p174/r4.anchor: وتسمى سورة القلم وسورة العلق وهي مكية بإجماعهم وهي أول ما نزل من القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r1.claim: Abu Ja'far reads the hamza lightly in both occurrences of اقرأ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر بتخفيف الهمزة في الحرفين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda treats the preposition bi as extra, yielding the sense 'read the name of your Lord.'
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة المعنى إقرأ باسم ربك والباء زائدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r3.claim: Exegetes explain the command as beginning one's recitation by invoking God's name.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r3.anchor: وقال المفسرون المعنى اذكر اسمه مستفتحا به قراءتك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r4.claim: The verse specifies the Creator because the idolaters knew God created, unlike their idols.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r4.anchor: وإنما قال تعالى الذي خلق لأن الكفار كانوا يعلمون أنه الخالق دون أصنامهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r1.claim: Aisha reports that revelation began with truthful dreams, after which the Prophet loved solitude and worshipped successive nights in Hira, returning to Khadija for provisions before another retreat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says the angel came to him in Hira and commanded him to read; three times the angel embraced him tightly, then recited the opening verses through 'what he did not know'. Both Sahih collections transmit the report through al-Zuhri.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "فقلت: ما أنا بقارئ". قال: "فأخذني فغطني حتى بلغ مني الجهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r3.speaker: خديجة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r3.claim: Khadija reassures Muhammad that God will never disgrace him because he maintains kinship, speaks truth, bears others' burdens, hosts guests, and helps people facing hardship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r3.anchor: فزملوه حتى ذهب عنه الروع. فقال: يا خديجة، ما لي: فأخبرها الخبر وقال: "قد خشيت علي". فقالت له: كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r4.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r4.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the same heavenly messenger sent to Moses and predicts Muhammad's people will drive him out; he vows support if alive then.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r4.anchor: فقال ورقة: هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى (4) ليتني (5) فيها جذعا أكون حيا حين يخرجك قومك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r5.claim: After Waraqa soon dies, revelation pauses; the Prophet is reported to grieve and repeatedly approach mountain peaks, but Gabriel confirms he is truly God's Messenger, calming him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p436#2/r5.anchor: فكلما أوفى بذروة جبل لكي يلقي نفسه منه، تبدى له جبريل فقال: يا محمد، إنك رسول الله حقا.

FARRA:v3p278/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r1.claim: The command “Read in the name of your Lord who created” was the first Qur’an revealed to the Prophet.
FARRA:v3p278/r1.anchor:
(1) .
هذا أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه من القرآن.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has seventeen verses.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r2.speaker: أبي عن النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r2.claim: Whoever recites Sūrat Iqraʾ is like one who recites the entire Mufaṣṣal section.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r2.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ (اقرأ باسم ربك) فكأنما قرأ المفصل كله

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r3.claim: Because the preceding surah ended by calling God the wisest of judges, this one begins by commanding mention of His name.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r3.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (والتين) بأنه أحكم الحاكمين، افتتح هذه السورة بالأمر بذكر اسمه

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r5.claim: Qirāʾa means recitation and is associated with gathering, as in gathering water in a basin.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r5.anchor: القراءة: التلاوة، وأصله الجمع، ومنه: قرأت الماء في الحوض،

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.speaker: عائشة ومجاهد وعطاء بن يسار
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.claim: One report says the first revelation from the Qur'an was Iqraʾ bismi rabbik.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.anchor: قيل: أول ما نزل من القرآن: (اقرأ باسم ربك)، عن عائشة، ومجاهد، وعطاء بن يسار.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.claim: Another report says the first five verses descended first, while the rest of the surah came later; a similar report is attributed to ʿĀʾisha.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.anchor: وقيل: أول ما نزل منها خمس آيات إلى قوله: (ما لم يعلم)، ثم نزل باقي السورة بعد ذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r12.claim: One chronology says al-Muddaththir followed the first revelation when the Prophet returned to Khadīja asking to be covered, then al-Qalam through its praise of his character and later al-Ḍuḥā; Ibn Shaddād reports Iqraʾ then a pause then al-Ḍuḥā.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r12.anchor: وقيل: نزل بعده: (ياأيها المدثر)، وذلك أنه لما أتاه الوحي رجع إلى خديجة متغيرا،

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r1.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r1.claim: ʿAmr ibn Shurahbīl says the first revealed surah was al-Fātiḥa; the author rejects this because consensus holds Iqraʾ was first.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r1.anchor: وقيل: أول سورة نزلت (فاتحة الكتاب)، عن عمرو بن شرحبيل. وليس بشيء؛ لأن الإجماع على أن أول ما نزل

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r2.claim: A report has Gabriel say “Read,” the Prophet ask what he should read, and Gabriel answer, “Read in the name of your Lord.”
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r2.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن جبريل قال له: اقرأ، فقال: وما أقرأ، قال: اقرأ باسم ربك.

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r3.claim: After this surah descended, the Prophet told Ubayy that Gabriel had ordered him to recite it to him.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r3.anchor: وروي أنه لما نزلت هذه السورة جاء رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلى أبي قال: أمرني جبريل أن أقرأ عليك.

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r4.claim: Read by beginning the Qur'an with God's name, then proceed to recite.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r4.anchor: استفتح باسم الله قراءة القرآن، فأمره بالابتداء بذكره، ثم بالقراءة، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r5.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r5.claim: Another interpretation is to read in the name of the Lord who revealed the recitation to you.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r5.anchor: وقيل: اقرأ باسم ربك المنزل عليك، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r6.claim: Honoring a name honors its referent because a name identifies what it uniquely signifies; God's name also expresses praise, honor, and glorification.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r6.anchor: لأن الاسم ذكر الشيء بما يخصه فلا سبيل إلى تعظيمه إلا بمعناه

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r7.claim: God created things in measured form under His wisdom.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r7.anchor: الذي خلق الأشياء مقدرا تحت حكمته، وعلى ما أراد خلق الإنسان من علق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say al-Alaq was the first sura revealed, though most commentators put al-Fatiha first and al-Qalam second.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد : هي أول سورة نزلت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r2.claim: The preposition in “in your Lord's name” is circumstantial: begin by saying bismillah, then read.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r2.anchor: محل { باسم ربك } النصب على الحال ، أي : اقرأ مفتتحا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r3.claim: The unexpressed object of created may be omitted to stress God as sole creator, or be all things universally.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r3.anchor: إما أن لا يقدر له مفعول وأن يراد أنه الذي حصل منه الخلق

MAJAZ:v2p304/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p304/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p304/r1.claim: Iqraʾ bi-smi rabbik means ‘read the name of your Lord.’
MAJAZ:v2p304/r1.anchor: «اقرأ باسم ربك» (1) مجازه: اقرأ اسم ربك..

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r1.claim: Gabriel's first visit brought a patterned cloth; he pressed the Prophet and commanded him to recite three times, while Muhammad said he could not read.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r1.anchor: روي عن عبيد بن عمير قال : جاء جبريل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r2.claim: The command means to begin reciting in the name of the Lord who created.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r2.anchor: أي استفتح قراءتك باسم ربك الذي خلق

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r3.claim: God identifies Himself as Creator to distinguish Him from Quraysh's other deities, none of which created, and remove confusion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r3.anchor: لأن قريشا كانت تعبد آلهة ليس فيهم خالق غيره تعالى , فميز نفسه بذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r4.speaker: عائشة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r4.claim: Aisha says this was the first surah revealed, followed by al-Qalam, al-Muddaththir, and al-Duha.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r4.anchor: روت عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r8.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r8.claim: A report transmitted through Ata al-Khurasani gives an ordered revelation list: 85 Meccan surahs, then 27 Medinan, and omits al-Fatiha as far as the author knows; the author calls it the fullest account despite many disagreements.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r8.anchor: فكان أول ما نزل فيما بلغنا : ( اقرأ باسم ربك ) ثم ( ن والقلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r9.claim: Most scholars say al-Alaq was the first surah revealed; among differing chronology reports, the author finds the transmitted list fullest and most satisfying.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r9.anchor: وإذا كانت هذه أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الأكثرين فقد روي في ترتيب السور بمكة والمدينة أحاديث

MUQATIL:96:1-8/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r1.claim: Read in the name of your Lord means in the name of the One; the One who created refers to the human being.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid are reported to say that al-Alaq was the first surah revealed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد هى أول سورة نزلت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r2.speaker: الجمهور
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r2.claim: The majority instead say that al-Fatiha was first revealed, followed by al-Qalam.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r2.anchor: والجمهور على أن الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة القلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r3.claim: The phrase “in the name of your Lord” is an accusative circumstantial phrase: read beginning with God's name, as if instructed first to say the basmala and then read.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r3.anchor: محل باسم ربك النصب على الحال أى اقرأ مفتحا باسم ربك كانه قبل قل بسم الله ثم اقرأ

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r4.claim: The object of “created” is omitted either because the phrase means the sole source of creation, or because it means that He created everything, without reason to privilege one creature.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#4/r4.anchor: ولم يذكر لخلق مفعولا لأن المعنى الذى حصل منه الخلق واستأثر به لا خالق سواه

NAHHAS:v5p261/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v5p261/r1.claim: The Kufans parse iqraʾ as jussive; al-Farrāʾ supplies an omitted lām, while Basrans call it indeclinable because it does not resemble nouns.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r1.anchor: في موضع جزم على قول الكوفيين والعامل فيه عند الفراء لام محذوفة

NAHHAS:v5p261/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r2.speaker: أبو زيد والكسائي
NAHHAS:v5p261/r2.claim: Abū Zayd and al-Kisāʾī transmit iqraʾ with hamza substitution, comparable to the poetic form yebdaʾ.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r2.anchor: وحكى أبو زيد والكسائي ( اقر ) على بدل الهمزة

NAHHAS:v5p261/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r3.speaker: زهير
NAHHAS:v5p261/r3.claim: Zuhayr's line إن لا يبد بالظلم يظلم is cited as a parallel for the hamza-substitution reading.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r3.anchor: ومثل هذا قول زهير ( وإن لا يبد بالظلم يظلم )

NAHHAS:v5p261/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r4.claim: The same explanation has been offered for the reading at 2:61, deriving it from denāʾah, lowliness.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r4.anchor: وقد قيل إن على هذا قراءة الجماعة

NAHHAS:v5p261/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r5.claim: Alladhī khalaqa may be genitive as an adjective of rabb, nominative with an implied subject, or accusative meaning I mean.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r5.anchor: ( الذي خلق ) في موضع خفض نعت لربك أو في موضع رفع على إضمار مبتدأ

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r1.claim: Most commentators hold that this sura was the first revelation: Gabriel brought its first five verses to Muhammad at Hira; alternatives name al-Muddaththir, al-Fatiha, or al-An'am 6:151, but the first view is correct.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r1.anchor: هذه السورة أول ما نزل من القرآن في قول معظم المفسرين

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r2.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r2.claim: Aisha reports that true dreams began the revelation, followed by the angel's first recitation of the opening verses; Bukhari records it.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r2.anchor: قالت عائشة: أول ما بدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الرؤيا الصادقة فجاءه الملك

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r3.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r3.claim: The sound report in both collections describes the Prophet's retreat to Hira, the angel's three embraces when he answered that he could not read, and the revelation of the first five verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r3.anchor: أول ما بدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r4.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r4.claim: Abu Raja says Abu Musa taught them this sura in Basra's mosque and identifies it as the first sura revealed to Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1/r4.anchor: وقال أبو رجاء العطاردي: وكان أبو موسى الأشعري يطوف علينا في هذا المسجد: مسجد البصرة،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r1.claim: The sequence attributed to Aisha is al-Alaq, al-Qalam, al-Muddaththir, then al-Duha, as cited by al-Mawardi.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r2.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri transmits that revelation first ran through the words what he did not know; frightened, the Prophet climbed mountain heights until Gabriel reassured him that he was a prophet, after which he returned to Khadija and asked to be covered and given cold water.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r2.anchor: أول ما نزل سورة: { اقرأ باسم ربك } إلى قوله { ما لم يعلم }

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r3.claim: Read in the name of the Lord means beginning recitation of the revelation with God's name, including the basmala at the start of each sura; grammatically the prepositional phrase is circumstantial accusative.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى { اقرأ باسم ربك } أي اقرأ ما أنزل إليك من القرآن مفتتحا باسم ربك،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r4.claim: Another analysis takes the bā' as meaning on, with the object omitted: read the Qur'an and begin it in God's name.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: الباء بمعنى على، أي اقرأ على اسم ربك.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r5.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r5.claim: Some say the name of the Lord is the Qur'an itself and the bā' is extra, as in the phrase about a tree growing with oil and the cited poem about reading suras.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r5.anchor: وقال قوم: اسم ربك هو القرآن، فهو يقول: { اقرأ باسم ربك } أي اسم ربك،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r6.claim: A further interpretation is simply to invoke God's name and begin recitation with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:1#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: معنى «اقرأ باسم ربك» أي اذكر اسمه. أمره أن يبتدىء القراءة باسم الله.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r1.claim: Qutb says the sura's opening was the first revelation by consensus; accounts assigning that primacy elsewhere are unreliable.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r1.anchor: مطلع هذه السورة هو أول ما نزل من القرآن باتفاق . والروايات التي تذكر نزول غيرها ابتداء ليست وثيقة

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r2.speaker: عائشة
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r2.claim: In the report Qutb says is recorded in both Sahih collections, Aisha recounts true dreams preceding revelation, solitary worship at Hira, Gabriel's three commands to read, and the first five verses.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r2.anchor: عن عائشة - رضي الله عنها - قالت :

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r3.speaker: خديجة
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r3.claim: Khadija comforts the frightened Prophet, assuring him God will never disgrace him because he keeps kinship, speaks truth, bears others' burdens, hosts guests, and helps in crises.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r3.anchor: فقالت له : كلا . أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r4.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r4.claim: After hearing the account, Waraka identifies the angel as the same messenger sent to Moses and says the Prophet will be driven out; those bringing such a message are opposed, and he promises support.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r4.anchor: فقال ورقة : هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى . ليتني فيها جذع

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r5.claim: Al-Tabari's report from Ibn al-Zubayr recounts the Prophet's alternate account: an angel brought written silk during sleep, recited the opening passage, and left it inscribed in his heart; later Gabriel appeared in the sky and identified himself.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير . قال :

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq also transmits a longer version of the revelation account through Wahb ibn Kaysan from Ubayd.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r6.anchor: وقد رواه ابن إسحاق مطولا عن وهب بن كيسان عن عبيد أيضا

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r7.claim: The event is immense in fact, meaning, and effect: God chose a human to receive His light, wisdom, words, and intended measure for humanity.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r7.anchor: قد تكرم - في عليائه - فالتفت إلى هذه الخليقة المسماة بالإنسان

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r8.claim: The event displays God's overflowing grace and mercy, given without cause beyond His generous nature; being remembered and addressed by God is an honor humans could never repay.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r8.anchor: يفيض من عطائه ورحمته بلا سبب ولا علة ، سوى أن الفيض والعطاء بعض صفاته

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r9.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r9.claim: Revelation redirected history by turning human conscience from earthly desires and standards toward heaven and divine revelation.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r10.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r10.claim: For twenty-three years believers experienced an immediate, direct connection with the heavenly realm, awaiting revelations that resolved their concerns and guided their steps; its distance from earthly sources was immense.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r10.anchor: فترة الثلاثة والعشرين عاما التالية ، التي استمرت فيها هذه الصلة الظاهرة المباشرة بين البشر والملأ الأعلى

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r11.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r11.speaker: أنس
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r11.claim: Anas reports that after the Prophet died, Abu Bakr and Umar visited Umm Ayman; she wept because revelation from heaven had ceased, and they wept with her. Qutb says Muslim recorded it.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r11.anchor: عن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال : قال أبو بكر لعمر

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r12.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r12.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r12.claim: Revelation's effects endure: people derive values from heaven and law from revelation rather than earth or desire, and the event decisively changed human history.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r12.anchor: لقد ولد الإنسان من جديد باستمداد قيمه من السماء لا من الأرض

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r13.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r13.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r13.claim: The divine method became clear and established as a decisive criterion, so people now stray knowingly and deliberately rather than through ambiguity.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r13.anchor: وتبينت خطوطه ومعالمه . ( ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيا من حي عن بينة )

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r14.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r14.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r14.claim: Only the opening passage dates to the first revelation; the sura's later portions refer to the Prophet's subsequent preaching, public worship, and pagan opposition, yet form a coherent ordered whole.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r14.anchor: فأما بقيتها فواضح أنها نزلت فيما بعد . فهي تشير إلى مواقف وحوادث في السيرة

QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r15.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r15.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r15.claim: As the Qur'an's first sura, it begins with God and directs the Prophet at the first heavenly contact and first step of his mission to read in God's name, beginning with the Creator.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:1/r15.anchor: وتوجه الرسول [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أول ما توجه ، في أول لحظة من لحظات اتصاله بالملأ الأعلى

RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda treats the bāʾ as extra, so the phrase means 'read the name of your Lord'; al-Akhtal's line uses bāʾ before 'the surahs' as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الباء زائدة ، والمعنى : اقرأ اسم ربك ، كما قال الأخطل

RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r2.claim: Razi rejects the extra-bāʾ reading: the Prophet's 'I am not a reader' would not answer an instruction to invoke God, the command would be redundant, and it needlessly discards the bāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r2.anchor: أحدها : أنه لو كان معناه اذكر اسم ربك ما حسن منه أن يقول : ما أنا بقارىء

RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r3.claim: Qirāʾa here means reciting the Qur'an, as supported by commands elsewhere to follow and recite it to people gradually.
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r3.anchor: القول الثاني : أن المراد من قوله : { اقرأ } أي اقرأ القرآن ، إذ القراءة لا تستعمل إلا فيه

RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r4.claim: Reading with God's name may mean beginning with the basmala, parsed adverbially; Razi says this supports requiring it at the start of every surah against those who omit it.
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r4.anchor: أحدها : أن يكون محل باسم ربك النصب على الحال فيكون التقدير : اقرأ القرآن مفتتحا باسم ربك

RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r5.claim: Alternatively, the basmala is an instrument of seeking God's help, as writing is done with a pen, especially when the Prophet said he could not read.
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r5.anchor: أن يكون المعنى اقرأ القرآن مستعينا باسم ربك كأنه يجعل الاسم آلة فيما يحاوله

RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r6.claim: Reading in God's name can mean dedicating the act to Him; invoking God's ownership also deters Satan from sharing a meal, and a neutral act can become worship when it supports obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v32p14/r6.anchor: أي اجعل هذا الفعل لله وافعله لأجله كما تقول : بنيت هذه الدار باسم الأمير

RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r1.claim: Although Allah is a loftier name than rabb, the command uses Lord because worship follows divine acts, not the bare attributes of essence; the title also reassures a frightened Prophet that his nurturer will complete His care.
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r1.anchor: وجوابه : أنه أمر بالعبادة ، وبصفات الذات ، وهو لا يستوجب شيئا ، وإنما يستوجب العبادة بصفات الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r2.claim: Calling God 'your Lord' may signal His care for the servant; alternatively, God's benefit flows to the servant first, and after obedience He names him 'My servant.'
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r2.anchor: تارة يضيف ذاته إليه بالربوبية كما ههنا ، وتارة يضيفه إلى نفسه بالعبودية ، أسرى بعبده

RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r3.claim: The phrase 'who created' answers how He is Muhammad's Lord: Muhammad was once nonexistent and then created, so a creator gave him existence and nurtured him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p15/r3.anchor: لأنك كنت بذاتك وصفاتك معدوما . ثم صرت موجودا فلا بد لك في ذاتك وصفاتك من خالق

RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.claim: Creation of the clot-grown human provides rational proof of power, wisdom, knowledge, and mercy; teaching by the pen points to revealed rulings known through transmission, so knowledge of lordship precedes and grounds prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى الدلالة العقلية الدالة على كمال القدرة والحكمة والعلم والرحمة

SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r1.claim: The common reading has a quiescent hamza as an imperative from reading; ʿĀṣim in al-Aʿshā's transmission opens rāʾ as if hamza became alif and was deleted in the imperative, with a poetic parallel.
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r1.anchor: العامة على سكون الهمزة أمرا من القراءة. وقرأ عاصم في رواية الأعشى براء مفتوحة

SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes bi-smi as circumstantial: begin by invoking your Lord's name, then recite.
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r2.anchor: أن تكون الباء للحال، أي: اقرأ مفتتحا باسم ربك، قل باسم الله، ثم اقرأ، قاله الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda offers an extra bāʾ, yielding read the name of your Lord, or treats the name as an added expression meaning remember your Lord.

SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r4.claim: The bāʾ may mark seeking aid, with an omitted object: recite what is revealed to you while seeking help through your Lord's name.
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r4.anchor: أن الباء للاستعانة والمفعول محذوف تقديره: اقرأ ما يوحى إليك مستعينا باسم ربك.

SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash makes bāʾ mean ʿalā, as in ride upon it in God's name, citing 11:41.
SAMIN-DURR:96:1/r5.anchor:
أنها بمعنى " على " ، أي: اقرأ على اسم ربك كما في قوله:
وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله

SAMIN-DURR:96:1#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:1#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:1#2/r1.claim: The second khalaqa may explain the first, initially leaving the creation unspecified and then singling out human creation to magnify it.
SAMIN-DURR:96:1#2/r1.anchor: ثم فسره ثانيا بخلق الإنسان تفخيما لخلق الإنسان.

SAMIN-DURR:96:1#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:1#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:1#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the first verb omits its object, understood universally as all things, since it is unqualified.
SAMIN-DURR:96:1#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حذف المفعول من الأول، تقديره: خلق كل شيء لأنه مطلق فيتناول كل مخلوق

STUDYQURAN:96:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r1.claim: The first mention of creation may mean that God creates all existence from nothing.
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r1.anchor: The first mention of creation in v. 1 can be taken as a reference to the fact that God creates all that exists from nothing

TAB:96:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r4.claim: Aisha recounts true dreams, Muhammad's retreat at Hira, Gabriel's arrival and repeated command to read, and identifies these opening verses as the first revelation.
TAB:96:3/r4.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت :  كان أوّل ما ابتدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة

TAB:96:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r5.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r5.claim: In Aisha's report, Khadija reassures Muhammad by citing his virtues; Waraqa identifies the revelation as Moses' angel, predicts opposition, and vows support if alive.
TAB:96:3/r5.anchor: فَقَالَتْ :  أبْشِرْ ،   فَوَاللّهِ لا يُخْزيكَ اللّهُ أبَدا ،   وَوَاللّهِ إنّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرّحَمِ

TAB:96:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r6.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r6.claim: Aisha's account says that after Iqra the next revelations included Nun, the Pen, al-Muddaththir, and al-Duha.
TAB:96:3/r6.anchor: ثُمّ كانَ أوّلُ ما نَزَلَ عَليّ مِنَ القُرآنِ بَعْدَ «اقْرأْ » :  ( ن والقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ

TAB:96:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB:96:3/r7.claim: Ibn Shaddad reports Gabriel's reading of the opening passage, Khadija's reassurance and referral to Waraqa, then delayed revelation and al-Duha's reassurance.
TAB:96:3/r7.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن شدّاد ،   قال :  أتى جبريل محمدا ،   فقال :  يا محمد اقرأ

TAB:96:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r8.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r8.claim: Aisha, through ʿUrwa and al-Zuhri, is cited as saying the first thing revealed was ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created.’
TAB:96:3/r8.anchor: عن عائشة قال إبراهيم :  قال سفيان :  حفظه لنا ابن إسحاق :  إن أوّل شيء أُنزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r9.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r9.claim: A further report from Aisha says the first surah revealed was Iqra bi-smi rabbika.
TAB:96:3/r9.anchor: عن عائشة ،   أنّ أوّل سورة أُنزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r10.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB:96:3/r10.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the first surah sent down to the Messenger was Iqra bi-smi rabbika alladhi khalaq.
TAB:96:3/r10.anchor: عن عُبيد بن عُمير ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r11.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB:96:3/r11.claim: Abu Raja says he learned Iqra from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari and identifies it as Muhammad's first revealed surah.
TAB:96:3/r11.anchor: أبو رجاء العُطارديّ ،   قال :  كنا في المسجد الجامع ،   ومقرئنا أبو موسى الأشعريّ

TAB:96:3/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r12.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB:96:3/r12.claim: ʿAta ibn Yasar says Iqra was the first surah revealed from the Qur'an.
TAB:96:3/r12.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r13.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:3/r13.claim: Mujahid says Iqra was the first Qur'anic revelation; one transmission adds that Nun and the Pen followed.
TAB:96:3/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قال :  أوّل ما نزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ وزاد ابن مهديّ :  ن والْقَلَمِ

TAB:96:4/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:4/r4.claim: Aisha recounts true dreams, Muhammad's retreat at Hira, Gabriel's arrival and repeated command to read, and identifies these opening verses as the first revelation.
TAB:96:4/r4.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت :  كان أوّل ما ابتدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة

TAB:96:4/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r5.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:4/r5.claim: In Aisha's report, Khadija reassures Muhammad by citing his virtues; Waraqa identifies the revelation as Moses' angel, predicts opposition, and vows support if alive.
TAB:96:4/r5.anchor: فَقَالَتْ :  أبْشِرْ ،   فَوَاللّهِ لا يُخْزيكَ اللّهُ أبَدا ،   وَوَاللّهِ إنّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرّحَمِ

TAB:96:4/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r6.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:4/r6.claim: Aisha's account says that after Iqra the next revelations included Nun, the Pen, al-Muddaththir, and al-Duha.
TAB:96:4/r6.anchor: ثُمّ كانَ أوّلُ ما نَزَلَ عَليّ مِنَ القُرآنِ بَعْدَ «اقْرأْ » :  ( ن والقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ

TAB:96:4/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB:96:4/r7.claim: Ibn Shaddad reports Gabriel's reading of the opening passage, Khadija's reassurance and referral to Waraqa, then delayed revelation and al-Duha's reassurance.
TAB:96:4/r7.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن شدّاد ،   قال :  أتى جبريل محمدا ،   فقال :  يا محمد اقرأ

TAB:96:4/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r8.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:4/r8.claim: Aisha, through ʿUrwa and al-Zuhri, is cited as saying the first thing revealed was ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created.’
TAB:96:4/r8.anchor: عن عائشة قال إبراهيم :  قال سفيان :  حفظه لنا ابن إسحاق :  إن أوّل شيء أُنزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:4/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r9.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:4/r9.claim: A further report from Aisha says the first surah revealed was Iqra bi-smi rabbika.
TAB:96:4/r9.anchor: عن عائشة ،   أنّ أوّل سورة أُنزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:4/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r10.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB:96:4/r10.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the first surah sent down to the Messenger was Iqra bi-smi rabbika alladhi khalaq.
TAB:96:4/r10.anchor: عن عُبيد بن عُمير ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:4/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r11.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB:96:4/r11.claim: Abu Raja says he learned Iqra from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari and identifies it as Muhammad's first revealed surah.
TAB:96:4/r11.anchor: أبو رجاء العُطارديّ ،   قال :  كنا في المسجد الجامع ،   ومقرئنا أبو موسى الأشعريّ

TAB:96:4/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r12.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB:96:4/r12.claim: ʿAta ibn Yasar says Iqra was the first surah revealed from the Qur'an.
TAB:96:4/r12.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:4/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:4/r13.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:4/r13.claim: Mujahid says Iqra was the first Qur'anic revelation; one transmission adds that Nun and the Pen followed.
TAB:96:4/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قال :  أوّل ما نزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ وزاد ابن مهديّ :  ن والْقَلَمِ

TAB-FULL:v24p527#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p527#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p527#2/r1.claim: God commands Muḥammad to recite while invoking the Creator.
TAB-FULL:v24p527#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق} [العلق: 1] قرأ حتى بلغ {علم بالقلم} [العلق: 4]

TAB-FULL:v24p527#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p527#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v24p527#2/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha narrates that Muḥammad's first revelation began with truthful dreams, retreat at Ḥirāʾ, and Gabriel commanding him to read; Khadīja comforted him and Waraqa identified the messenger as the angel sent to Moses.
TAB-FULL:v24p527#2/r3.anchor: عن عائشة، أنها قالت: كان أول ما أبتدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة

TAB-FULL:v24p530/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r1.claim: A report says Gabriel commanded Muḥammad to read through the verse about teaching what was unknown; he feared something had happened, Khadīja reassured him, and later the pause in revelation led to the opening verses of Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā.
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r1.anchor: قال: ثنا عبد الله بن شداد، قال: أتى جبريل محمدا، فقال: يا محمد اقرأ، فقال: «وما أقرأ؟»

TAB-FULL:v24p530/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r2.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r2.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha, preserved through Ibn Isḥāq, says 'Read in the name of your Lord' was the first revelation.
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r2.anchor: عن الزهري، عن عروة، عن عائشة، قال إبراهيم: قال سفيان: حفظه لنا ابن إسحاق: إن أول شيء أنزل من القرآن

TAB-FULL:v24p530/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r3.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r3.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr also identifies this as the first sūra revealed to the Messenger.
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار، عن عبيد بن عمير، قال: أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأ باسم ربك

TAB-FULL:v24p530/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r4.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r4.claim: Abū Rajāʾ says he learned the opening sūra from Abū Mūsā, who recited it in Basra, and that it was the first sūra revealed.
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r4.anchor: قال: أخبرنا أبو رجاء العطاردي، قال: كنا في المسجد الجامع، ومقرئنا أبو موسى الأشعري

TAB-FULL:v24p531/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r1.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār says the first sūra revealed from the Qurʾān was 'Read in the name of your Lord.'
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار، قال: أول سورة نزلت من القرآن اقرأ باسم ربك

TAB-FULL:v24p531/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the first revelation was 'Read in the name of your Lord'; Ibn Mahdī's version adds Sūrat al-Qalam.
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قال: أول ما نزل من القرآن: اقرأ باسم ربك وزاد ابن مهدي: ن والقلم

TAB-FULL:v24p531/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r3.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r3.claim: Abū Rajāʾ says he learned the opening sūra from Abū Mūsā and identifies it as the first revealed to Muḥammad.
TAB-FULL:v24p531/r3.anchor: عن قرة بن خالد، عن أبي رجاء العطاردي، قال: إني لأنظر إلى أبي موسى وهو يقرأ القرآن في مسجد البصرة

TABATABAI:96:1-2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r2.claim: Raghib defines recitation as joining letters and words in ordered reading, not merely gathering people or pronouncing a single letter.
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r2.anchor: قال الراغب والقراءة ضم الحروف والكلمات بعضها إلى بعض في الترتيل

TABATABAI:96:1-2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r3.claim: Qaraʾa can mean mentally combining written words, uttering them aloud, or reading them to another person; in the last sense it is also tilāwa.
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r3.anchor: يقال قرأت الكتاب إذا جمعت ما فيه من الحروف والكلمات بضم بعضها إلى بعض في الذهن

TABATABAI:96:1-2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r4.claim: The apparent sense of iqraʾ is to receive and read what the angel reveals; the command is embedded within the revealed book, like an instruction at a book’s opening.
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r4.anchor: من القرآن فالجملة أمر بقراءة الكتاب وهي من الكتاب

TABATABAI:96:1-2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r5.claim: The wording supports this being the first revelation and implies an omitted object, ‘the Qur’an’ or its equivalent.
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r5.anchor: وهذا السياق يؤيد أولا ما ورد أن الآيات أول ما نزل من القرآن

TABATABAI:96:1-2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r6.claim: The command does not simply use read intransitively with its object omitted, nor does it mean ‘recite to people’ with an omitted complement.
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r6.anchor: وليس المراد مطلق القراءة باستعمال { اقرأ } استعمال الفعل اللازم

TABATABAI:96:1-2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r7.claim: The phrase ‘in the name of your Lord’ is not the object of ‘read’ with an extra ba, yielding ‘read your Lord’s name’ or merely say the basmala.
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r7.anchor: ولا أن قوله { باسم ربك } مفعول { اقرأ } والباء زائدة

TABATABAI:96:1-2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r8.claim: ‘In the name of your Lord’ attaches to an implied ‘beginning’ or to ‘read’ with the ba of accompaniment; the basmala is part of the surah and God teaches by having the Prophet begin with it.
TABATABAI:96:1-2/r8.anchor: الباء للملابسة ولا ينافي ذلك كون البسملة المبتداة بها السورة جزء من السورة

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r1.claim: The implied exception is exemplified by the instruction not to say ‘I will do this tomorrow’ unless God wills.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r1.anchor: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r2.claim: ‘Your Lord who created’ asserts that lordship belongs to God alone, refuting polytheists who concede creation but assign governance to favored angels, jinn, or humans.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r2.anchor: فدفعه الله بقوله { ربك الذي خلق } الناص على أن الربوبية والخلق له وحده

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r1.claim: Tafsir reports that اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق was the first Qur'anic verse revealed.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r1.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن أول آية نزلت من القرآن (اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق).

TABRISI:96:2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r16.claim: The opening command tells the Prophet to recite in God's name and invoke Him by His beautiful names; honoring the name honors the named one, which only someone who knows God and believes in worship can truly do.
TABRISI:96:2/r16.anchor: هذا أمر من الله سبحانه لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقرأ باسم ربه

TABRISI:96:2#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2#2/r1.claim: The prefixed bi is extra in the command, which can be read as 'recite your Lord's name'; the source links the invocation of God or al-Rahman to His beautiful names.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r1.anchor: فالباء هنا زائدة والتقدير اقرأ باسم ربك

TABRISI:96:2#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r2.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
TABRISI:96:2#2/r2.claim: Most exegetes say this surah was the first Quran revelation; Gabriel first came to the Prophet on Hira and taught him its first five verses.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r2.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن هذه السورة أول ما نزل من القرآن وأول يوم نزل جبرائيل

TABRISI:96:2#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:96:2#2/r3.claim: An alternative says the first revelation was 'O you who are wrapped up'.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r3.anchor: أول ما نزل من القرآن قوله

TABRISI:96:2#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r4.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
TABRISI:96:2#2/r4.claim: An alternative report says the Opening was the first surah revealed: the Prophet told Khadija he heard a call in solitude; she reassured him, took him to Waraqa, who identified him as a prophet like Moses and foretold his mission and struggle. After Waraqa died, the Prophet said he saw him in Paradise in silk for believing him.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r4.anchor: رواه الحاكم أبو عبد الله الحافظ بإسناده عن أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لخديجة

TABRISI:96:2#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r5.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
TABRISI:96:2#2/r5.claim: Waraqa tells Khadija and the Prophet that Gabriel brings the revelation, that the Prophet is sent, and that he will be commanded to struggle; Waraqa promises to support him if alive.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r5.anchor: فلما خلا ناداه يا محمد قل له ذلك فقال له أبشر

TABRISI:96:2#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:96:2#2/r6.claim: After Waraqa's death, the Prophet said he saw the priest in Paradise wearing silk because he believed and affirmed him.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r6.anchor: لقد رأيت القس في الجنة عليه ثياب الحرير لأنه آمن بي وصدقني

TABRISI:96:2#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r7.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
TABRISI:96:2#2/r7.claim: Waraqa's poem calls Ahmad a messenger and says Gabriel and Michael bring revelation from God that expands the chest, sorting people between Paradise and Hell.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r7.anchor: فإن يك حقا يا خديجة فاعلمي حديثك إيانا فأحمد مرسل

THALABI:v10p242#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p242#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p242#3/r1.claim: ʿAlaq means a clinging blood clot, its singular is ʿalaqa, and “the human” is singular in wording but collective in meaning.
THALABI:v10p242#3/r1.anchor: خلق الإنسان من علق أي الدم، واحدتها علقة، وإنما جمع ولفظ الإنسان واحد، لأنه في معنى الجمع

THALABI:v10p242#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p242#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p242#3/r2.claim: Most scholars say this was the first surah revealed, with its first five verses the first revelation.
THALABI:v10p242#3/r2.anchor: وهذه أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن، وأول ما نزل منها خمس آيات من

THALABI:v10p242#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p242#3/r3.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v10p242#3/r3.claim: She recounts the first revelation: true dreams, retreat at Ḥirāʾ, Gabriel’s three forceful embraces and command to read, then the first five verses.
THALABI:v10p242#3/r3.anchor: عائشة أنها قالت: أول ما بدأ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

THALABI:v10p242#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p242#3/r4.speaker: خديجة
THALABI:v10p242#3/r4.claim: She reassured the frightened Prophet that God would not disgrace him because he maintained kinship, told the truth, bore burdens, hosted guests, and helped in times of need.
THALABI:v10p242#3/r4.anchor: كلا ابشر، فو الله لا يحزنك الله، إنك لتصل الرحم، وتصدق الحديث، وتحمل الكل

THALABI:v10p242#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p242#3/r5.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
THALABI:v10p242#3/r5.claim: After hearing the account, he identified the visitor as the same heavenly messenger sent to Moses and predicted that the Prophet’s people would expel and mistreat him; he promised support if alive.
THALABI:v10p242#3/r5.anchor: هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى، يا ليتني فيها جذع

THALABI:v10p242#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p242#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p242#3/r6.claim: After Waraqa died revelation paused; the Prophet became so distressed that he repeatedly approached mountain peaks intending to throw himself off, until Gabriel reassured him he was God’s true messenger.
THALABI:v10p242#3/r6.anchor: ثم لم ينشب ورقة ان توفي وفتر الوحي فترة، حتى حزن رسول الله

THALABI:v10p243/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p243/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v10p243/r1.claim: He reports the Prophet’s account of Gabriel appearing seated between heaven and earth after the first revelation, frightening him and prompting him to seek covering.
THALABI:v10p243/r1.anchor: فبينما أنا أمشي سمعت صوتا من السماء فرفعت رأسي

THALABI:v10p243/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p243/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p243/r3.claim: The sequence after “Read” and al-Muddaththir was al-Qalam through “you are of great character,” then al-Ḍuḥā.
THALABI:v10p243/r3.anchor: ثم كان ما نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن بعد اقرأ والمدثر، ن والقلم إلى قوله: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم، ثم

THALABI:v10p243/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p243/r5.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v10p243/r5.claim: She says the first surah revealed was “Read in the name of your Lord.”
THALABI:v10p243/r5.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: إن أول سورة نزلت اقرأ باسم ربك

THALABI:v10p243/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p243/r6.speaker: أبو موسى
THALABI:v10p243/r6.claim: A report from Abū Rajāʾ says Abū Mūsā taught this surah and held that al-Fātiḥa was the first surah revealed.
THALABI:v10p243/r6.anchor:
فعنه أخذت هذه السورة: اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق .
وقال: كانت أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله

THALABI:v10p243/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p243/r7.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
THALABI:v10p243/r7.claim: He reports that the Prophet told Khadīja he heard a voice when alone and feared that a momentous matter was happening.
THALABI:v10p243/r7.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لخديجة: «إني إذا خلوت وحدي سمعت نداء

THALABI:v10p244/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p244/r1.speaker: خديجة
THALABI:v10p244/r1.claim: She reassured the Prophet that God would not abandon him because he fulfilled trusts, maintained family ties, and spoke truthfully.
THALABI:v10p244/r1.anchor: فقالت: معاذ الله، ما كان الله عز وجل ليفعل بك ذاك، فو الله إنك لتؤدي الأمانة وتصل الرحم

THALABI:v10p244/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p244/r2.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
THALABI:v10p244/r2.claim: He tells the Prophet to stand still and listen when the voice calls, then report what it says.
THALABI:v10p244/r2.anchor: فقال له: لا تفعل، إذا أتاك فاثبت حتى تسمع ما يقول ثم ائتني فأخبرني

THALABI:v10p244/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p244/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p244/r3.claim: In this account, the voice tells the Prophet to recite the basmala and the opening of al-Fātiḥa through its final words, then affirm God’s oneness.
THALABI:v10p244/r3.anchor: فلما خلا ناداه يا محمد قل: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين حتى بلغ ولا الضالين قل: لا إله إلا الله

THALABI:v10p244/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p244/r4.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
THALABI:v10p244/r4.claim: He recognizes the Prophet as the one foretold by Jesus, a messenger like Moses, and predicts that he will be commanded to fight; Waraqa vows to join him.
THALABI:v10p244/r4.anchor:
فقال له ورقة: أبشر ثم أبشر فأنا
أشهد أنك الذي بشر به ابن مريم، وأنك على مثل ناموس موسى

THALABI:v10p244/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p244/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p244/r5.claim: The Prophet says he saw the Christian priest Waraqa in Paradise wearing silk because Waraqa believed and affirmed him.
THALABI:v10p244/r5.anchor: لقد رأيت القس في الجنة، عليه ثياب الحرير لأنه آمن بي وصدقني

THALABI:v10p244/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p244/r6.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
THALABI:v10p244/r6.claim: His poem says Aḥmad is a messenger, Gabriel and Michael bring revelation from God, and people divide into the saved and the doomed.
THALABI:v10p244/r6.anchor:
فإن يك حقا يا خديجة فاعلمي … حديثك إيانا فأحمد مرسل
وجبريل يأتيه وميكال معهما

ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n1/r1.claim: Iqra may mean read or recite; Asad prefers read because it denotes conscious reception aimed at understanding, whereas reciting can merely deliver memorized or written words aloud.
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n1/r1.anchor: the former rendering is, to my mind, by far the preferable in this context

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين وأهل التأويل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r1.claim: Most exegetes say this sūra was the first revelation: Gabriel came to Muḥammad at Ḥirāʾ and taught him its first five verses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين، وأهل التأويل على أن هذه السورة أول ما نزل من القرآن،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r2.claim: One grammatical reading treats the preposition bi as extra, so the phrase means “recite your Lord's name”; al-Akhṭal's line about women who “read by sūras” witnesses the construction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r2.anchor: {اقرأ باسم ربك} مجازه: اسم ربك) (¬1)، أن الباء زائدة (¬2) معناه: اقرأ اسم ربك،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means begin reciting by invoking the Lord's name; this supports saying the basmala at the opening of every sūra, as revealed, against those who omit it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p165#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى {اقرأ باسم ربك} اذكر اسمه كأنه أمران يبدأ (¬1) القراءة باسم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169/r1.claim: “The one who created” means all creatures.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169/r1.anchor: وقوله (¬1) {الذي خلق} وقال الكلبي: يعني الخلائق

WAHIDI-QT:96:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:1/r1.claim: “Read in your Lord's name” means reciting the Quran while invoking God at the start of every surah.
WAHIDI-QT:96:1/r1.anchor: وهو أن تذكر التسمية في ابتداء كل سورة

WAHIDI-QT:96:1/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:1/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:1/r2.claim: The One who created made all things and creatures.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r1.claim: Read the Qur'an in the name of God, meaning pronounce the basmala at the beginning of every sura.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r1.anchor: يعني: اقرأ القرآن باسم ربك، وهو أن تذكر التسمية في ابتداء كل سورة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r2.claim: The Creator made all things and creatures.

ELMALILI:96:1-8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r1.claim: The command means to begin reading in the name of the Lord, starting with God's exalted name.
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r1.anchor: Oku O Rabbinin ismiyle yani O’nun yüce adıyla, Allah ism-i celîli ile başlayarak oku

ELMALILI:96:1-8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r2.claim: At Hira the angel first commanded only “read” twice; because Muhammad had not read before, he answered that he was not a reader, so these were preparatory prompts to begin recitation.
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r2.anchor: o ilk iki ٱقْرَأْ emri henüz Kur’an değil, kıraat denilen fiile şurû‘için heceletme kabîlinden ihzârî bir emr ü teklif idi

ELMALILI:96:1-8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r3.claim: The third command began the Qur'an and simultaneously miraculously made the unreading Prophet able to read, fixed the text to be recited, and taught him to introduce the Creator, as related to 29:48 and 42:52.
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r3.anchor: Kur’an üçüncü defaki tazyikten sonra olan işbu ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ emriyle başlamıştı

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r1.claim: Recitation is audibly voicing connected words in sequence, whether from memory or a page and aloud or quietly; silent study and recollection are figurative senses.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r1.anchor: birbiri ardınca ağızdan sesle çıkarmaktır ki, gerek ezberden ve gerek yüzünden gerek hafî ve gerek celî mutlaka okumak demektir.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r2.claim: A book need not already be written to be a book, and reading does not require writing; the fullest recitation is from memory.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r2.anchor: Kitabın kitap olması için bilfiil yazılmış olması şart olmadığı gibi, okumak için de mutlaka yazı şart değildir

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r3.claim: A prophetic report says reading from a page is rewarded because it supports accurate retention and memorization.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r3.anchor: yüzünden okumanın sevab ve fazileti zabt u hıfza vesile olması itibariyledir.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r4.claim: The Prophet's own recitation was the fullest kind, from memory by divine instruction, whether for himself, prayer, teaching others, or dictation.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r4.anchor: Resûlullah’ın kıraati yazıya ihtiyâcı olmaksızın mintarafillah kendine böyle nâzil olan Kur’ân’ı hıfzından ekmel surette kıraattir

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r5.claim: The command miraculously gave the unlettered Prophet a book to recite, teach, and dictate without writing himself; beginning with the basmala accords with God's lordship.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r5.anchor: mukaddemâ hiç kitap okumamış, yazı yazmamış olan Nebiyy-i Ümmî’ye bu emir ile bir mucize olarak okunacak bir kitap verilmeye başlanmış

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r6.claim: The attachment to “your Lord” explains the command through God's role as creator and caretaker, leaving no doubt that He can teach an unlettered recipient.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r1.claim: Creation rationally points to knowledge of God, while recitation and writing transmit what the reader and writer received; the Qur'an includes rational proofs but chiefly signifies through its heard wording that the Prophet learned from God.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r1.anchor: Doğrudan doğru hilkati mütalaanın ma‘rifetullâha delâleti aklîdir. Kıraat ve kitabette ise okuyan ve yazandan nakil haysiyeti ile delâlet-i sem‘iye vardır

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r2.claim: It is significant that the first revealed verses unite rational and transmitted proof and present recitation, writing, and knowledge as great divine gifts; the pen also encourages the community to literacy.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r3.claim: The Prophet needed no writing to recite, while his unlettered reading establishes prophethood and the Qur'an's divine origin; 29:48 states this explicitly.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r3.anchor: Peygamber’in kıraat için yazıya ihtiyâcı olmadığı iş‘âr olunmakla beraber şüphe yok ki kalem ile tâlimin de büyük bir ikrâm-ı rabbânî olduğu beyan buyurulmuş

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r4.claim: The Prophet never wrote with his own hand and needed no writing to retain revelation because God promised he would not forget in 87:6; he recited and dictated the revelation to scribes for the community.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r4.anchor: hıfz u zabt için de yazmaya ihtiyâcı olmadığı, fakat nâzil olanı ümmetin hıfzı için vahiy kâtiblerine okuyup yazdırdığı mâlumdur.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r5.claim: The common view is that the Prophet did not learn to read others' writing; at Hudaybiyya, he famously asked Ali which word to erase.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r5.anchor: Nitekim Hudeybiye musâlahanâmesinde yazılan bir kelimeyi silmek için hangisi olduğunu Hazret-i Ali’ye sorduğu mâruftur.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r6.claim: Some accounts in al-Shifa and related works say the Prophet instructed his scribe Muawiya how to prepare the pen and beautify the basmala, suggesting knowledge of writing.
