ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r6.anchor: Şifâ ve etrafında mezkur olduğu üzere sonradan kâtibi Hazret-i Muaviye’ye أَلق الدَّوَاةَ وَحَرِّفِ الْقَلَمَ وَطَوِّلِ الْبَاءَ

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r7.claim: Elmalılı says such instructions may have come through special revelation and that learning writing during the twenty-three prophetic years is plausible, without compromising the miracle of becoming a reader while unlettered.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r7.anchor: sene Kur’ân’ı okumak ve yazdırmak vazifesi olmuş olan Hazret-i Peygamber’in bu müddet zarfında yazıyı da bellemiş olması müsteb‘ad değil, mâkuldür.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r8.claim: The Prophet's not writing or reading books before prophethood would support the claim in 29:48; after prophethood, learning script would confirm rather than undermine it, though he certainly wrote nothing himself or studied other books.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r8.anchor: Fakat bilfiil yazmadığı ve başka kitap mütalaa etmediği muhakkaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.claim: These were the first revelation; the command to read addresses Muhammad and all Muslims, and its repetition stresses the importance of reading and knowledge, through which humans are distinguished among living things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.anchor: İlk vahyin “oku” emriyle başlaması ve bu emrin iki defa tekrar edilmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r2.claim: The unspecified object of reading includes revelation, cosmic signs, and everything to study and understand for lessons and useful results; knowing the Creator is knowledge and religion's chief aim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r2.anchor: okunması yani üzerinde inceleme yapıp zihin yorarak hakkında bilgi edinilmesi, ders ve ibret alınması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r3.claim: Reading can mean in the Creator Lord's name or for the Creator; every reading or activity should begin with, serve, and seek help from God rather than another being.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r3.anchor: okumanın (veya herhangi bir faaliyetin) Allah’ın adıyla, Allah için ve Allah adına yapılması emredilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r4.claim: Creation is stressed because God made both human capacity for reading and the objects studied; denying God or gratitude while using these gifts is profound ingratitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r4.anchor: bütün bu lütufları görmezlikten gelerek Allah’a şükretmemek, O’nu tanımamak

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r1.claim: Qurʾān derives from qaraʾa, and the divine title rabb is treated in the note to 95:8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu dem von qaraʾa abgeleiteten Substantiv qurʾān vgl. die Anmerkung zu 75:16–19

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Hirschfeld 1902
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r2.claim: Hirschfeld recognizes a correspondence between iqraʾ bi-smi rabbika and the Hebrew formula qārāʾ be-šem YHWH, then proposes proclaim the name of your Lord.

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Nöldeke and Schwally
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r3.claim: Nöldeke and Schwally object that qaraʾa elsewhere in the Quran means recite from a text or memory, supporting the usual translation recite in the name of your Lord.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Nöldeke und Schwally zu Recht geltend, dass qaraʾa überall sonst im Koran „vortragen“

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r4.claim: Despite rejecting Hirschfeld's translation, the author allows that the phrase deliberately imitates a biblical expression, as 112:1 may echo Deuteronomy 6:4.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r4.anchor: die Nähe zur hebräischen Wortverbindung – die im Syrischen ganz parallel lautet – auf die bewusste Nachbildung einer biblischen Sprachfigur zurückgeht

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r5.claim: Isaiah 40:5 also addresses the prophet with qrā, corresponding to iqraʾ, so the Quranic preacher may be implicitly cast as a second Isaiah.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r5.anchor: 96:1 könnte sich damit an den auch liturgisch prominenten Jesaja-Passus anlehnen und den koranischen Verkünder implizit als zweiten Jesaja zeichnen

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r6.claim: The genitive name of your Lord occurs in related calls to glorification and praise throughout several suras.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r6.anchor: Die Genitivverbindung ʾism rabbika, „der Name deines Herrn“, erscheint in ähnlichen Aufrufen noch in 87:1

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r7.claim: The opening imperative follows hymn openings in Q 87, 73, and 74, and likely addresses the preacher; such commands also apply by example to the wider community of hearers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r7.anchor: Die Anrede iqraʾ zur Eröffnung des Hymnus entspricht

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p384/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p384/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p384/r1.claim: Iqraʾ can be a teacher's instruction to read, but it can also direct someone to read or recite aloud to others.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p384/r1.anchor: is not merely used to convey what a teacher would say to a student

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r1.claim: Qur'an 7:204 and 17:45 show that iqraʾ can mean reciting the Qur'an aloud to an audience; the usage is indicated by these verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r1.anchor: The indication to this usage is present within the verses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r2.claim: Reciting in the Creator's name presents the Qur'an as God's binding directive, not a preacher's words or a request; people must obey and not mock or trivialize it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r2.anchor: what is being recited out to them is directly from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r3.claim: The Qur'an is uniquely composed entirely of words revealed by God, so its opponents should recognize its exaltedness and fear its wrath.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r3.anchor: No other Book before it has the honour to be entirely composed of the words revealed by God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r4.claim: Earlier scriptures predict that Muhammad would speak in God's name and that God would hold accountable those rejecting his message.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p385/r4.anchor: whatever he will say, he will say in the name of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r1.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r1.claim: One reported view makes the whole of Sūrah al-‘Alaq the Qur’an’s first revelation; the majority instead regards its first five verses as first, based on a report in Bukhārī and Muslim.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r2.speaker: Zamakhsharī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r2.claim: Zamakhsharī records the view that al-Fātiḥah was revealed first and then Sūrah al-Qalam; exegetes both accept and dispute it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r2.anchor: Zamakhshar ī. He has recorded in

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r3.speaker: the proponents of this view
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r3.claim: A third view says Sūrah al-Muddaththir was first; its proponents probably mean only its opening verses because the rest has a severity resembling al-‘Alaq.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r3.anchor: The proponents of this view most probably regard its initial verses only as the first revelation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r4.claim: The author considers al-‘Alaq a coherent, single unit: its first five verses share the rest’s severe tone, and nothing in it indicates revelation in two episodes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r4.anchor: The tone of its first five verses is no different

QIRAAT-ER:96:1:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:96:1:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:96:1:1#1/r1.claim: In pause, Ibn Kathīr and others drop hamza, giving a long final a; this canonical reading softens the command phonetically.
QIRAAT-ER:96:1:1#1/r1.anchor: Ibn Kathir and others drop hamza in pause

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#3/r1.speaker: النبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#3/r1.claim: Reports from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār and al-Zuhrī say the first revelation came to the Prophet at Ḥirāʾ on a silk cloth bearing the opening of this sūra through ‘what he did not know.’
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#3/r1.anchor: عن معمر قال أخبرني عمرو بن دينار والزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#3/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#3/r2.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says this was the first sūra revealed to the Prophet.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#3/r2.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار قال سمعت عبيد بن عمير يقول أول سورة أنزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r4.claim: The majority read iqraʾ with a hamza; al-Aʿshāʾ, transmitting from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, drops it by analogy with the imperfect verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: اقرأ بهمزة ساكنة والأعشى، عن أبي بكر، عن عاصم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r5.claim: The bāʾ may mark an instrument or accompaniment, with an omitted object meaning “read what is revealed”; alternatively God’s name is the object, or one reads the basmala at each sūra’s opening.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r5.anchor: والظاهر تعلق الباء باقرأ وتكون للاستعانة، ومفعول اقرأ محذوف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r6.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash takes bāʾ as “upon,” as in the command to board the ark in God’s name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r6.anchor: وقال الأخفش: الباء بمعنى على، أي اقرأ على اسم الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes “in the name of your Lord” a circumstantial accusative: begin by saying the basmala, then read; Abū Ḥayyān notes the analysis is also attributed to Qatāda.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: محل باسم ربك النصب على الحال، أي اقرأ مفتتحا باسم ربك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda regards the bāʾ as extra, meaning “mention your Lord”; he also regards “name” as extra, yielding “read with your Lord’s aid.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الباء صلة، والمعنى اذكر ربك. وقال أيضا: الاسم صلة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r9.claim: The choice of “your Lord” evokes the one who nurtured and cared for the Prophet; direct address indicates exclusive intimacy, with no lord for him but God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r9.anchor: وجاء باسم ربك، ولم يأت بلفظ الجلالة لما في لفظ الرب من معنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r10.claim: Calling God Creator excludes the idols that Arabs called lords; the unexpressed object is universal, meaning that He created everything.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p506/r10.anchor: ثم جاء بصفة الخالق، وهو المنشئ للعالم لما كانت العرب تسمي الأصنام أربا.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p167/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p167/r1.speaker: الطيالسي، الحارث، أبو نعيم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p167/r1.claim: Reports in the Musnads of al-Tayalisi and al-Harith and in Abu Nuaym say Gabriel and Michael split Muhammad's chest and washed it before Gabriel told him to read the opening revelation.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r1.claim: Surat Iqra is Meccan without dispute, but its verse count differs: twenty in the Hijazi count, nineteen Iraqi, and eighteen Syrian.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r1.anchor: وتسمى سورة اقرأ لا خلاف في مكيتها وإنما الخلاف في عدد آيها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r2.claim: Many say Iqra was the first revelation; Abu Musa's student Abu Raja reports that Abu Musa called it the first surah sent to Muhammad.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r2.anchor: أخرج الطبراني في الكبير بسنده على شرط الصحيح عن أبي رجاء العطاردي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r3.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r3.claim: Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi authenticate a report from Aisha likewise identifying Iqra as first; Mujahid says it was followed by Nun and the pen.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r3.anchor: وقد أخرج الحاكم في المستدرك والبيهقي في الدلائل وصححاه عن عائشة نحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r4.claim: A report from Jabir calls Ya ayyuhal-Muddaththir the first revelation, but the earlier group offers several responses to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r4.anchor: وروي الشيخان عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن قال سألت جابر بن عبد الله أي القرآن أنزل أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r5.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r5.claim: A trustworthy-transmitters but mursal report argues that al-Fatiha came first; the response is that it could refer to what followed Iqra and Muddaththir, and other reports are stronger.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r5.anchor: وقيل الفاتحة واحتج له بحديث مرسل رجاله ثقات أخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r6.speaker: جابر بن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r6.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd gives the order Iqra, Nun, al-Muzzammil, al-Muddaththir, then al-Fatiha.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r6.anchor: وجزم جابر بن زيد بأن أول ما نزل اقرأ ثم ن ثم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r7.claim: Another view holds that only the opening of Iqra through what he did not know was revealed first and the remainder came later, as suggested by Aisha's account of the first revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p177#3/r7.anchor: وقيل أول ما نزل صدرها إلى ما لم يعلم في غار حراء ثم نزل آخرها بعد ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r1.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r1.claim: Aisha’s account says revelation paused soon after the opening verses; a report from Jabir then recounts how revelation resumed with al-Muddaththir.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r1.anchor: قالت ثم لم ينشب ورفة أن توفي وفتر الوحي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r2.claim: Jabir's account of Muddaththir explicitly concerns the period after revelation paused and then resumed, undermining its use as the first revelation overall.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r2.anchor: ويعلم منه ضعف الأستدلال على كون سورة المدثر أول نازل من القرآن على الإطلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r3.claim: Al-Alusi follows the view that the opening of Iqra was the first revelation outright, supported by Aisha's highly authentic report; ما أنا بقارئ is a statement of inability, not refusal, which would otherwise be grave disobedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r3.anchor: الصحيح كما قال البعض وهو الذي اختاره إن صدر هذه السورة الكريمة هو أول ما أنزل من القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r4.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r4.claim: Al-Kashf takes Jabir's claim to concern the first complete surah, while Sahih Muslim's commentary distinguishes Iqra as first overall from Muddaththir as first after the hiatus; the claim that al-Fatiha came first is plainly false.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r4.anchor: وفي الكشف الوجه حمل قول جابر على السورة الكاملة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r5.claim: The preceding surah described humanity's best form; this surah explains its material origin in clinging blood and expands on its afterlife condition, linking the two surahs thematically.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r5.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه في سورة التين خلق الإنسان في أحسن تقويم بين عز وجل هنا أنه تعالى خلق الإنسان من علق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r1.claim: Read has an implied object, what is revealed of the Quran; the verb is not intransitive and باسم ربك is not its object with an extra ba, contrary to Abu Ubayda.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r1.anchor: إقرأ أي ما يوحى إليك من القرآن مقدر بقرينة المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda treats the ba as extra and reads the command as Remember your Lord; al-Alusi rejects this, taking the ba as original accompaniment attached to read or an implied circumstantial phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r2.anchor: بل هي أصلية ومعناها الملابسة وهي متعلقة بما عندها أو بمحذوف وقع حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r3.claim: According to a reading attributed to Qatada, the command means begin or open with your Lord's name, saying the basmala and then reading; this supports requiring basmala when reading and has been used to argue it belongs to every surah, though al-Alusi notes debate.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r3.anchor: كما روي عن قتادة والمعنى اقرأ مبتدئا أو مفتتحا باسم ربك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r4.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r4.claim: Some argue that the basmala is not Quran at the beginnings of surahs because it is absent from sound accounts of the first revelation; al-Nawawi reports this argument, while proponents answer that it descended later.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r4.anchor: وبعضهم استدل على أنها ليست بقرآن في أوائل السور بأنها لم تذكر فيما صح من أخبار بدء الوحي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة، الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r5.claim: Ikrima and Hasan say the basmala was the first Quranic revelation; al-Dahhak's report from Ibn Abbas says Gabriel first instructed Muhammad to seek refuge and say it. Al-Suyuti counts this as the first revelation, but al-Alusi objects that this does not follow.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r5.anchor: وهذا خلاف ما أخرج الواحدي عن عكرمة والحسن أنهما قالا أول ما نزل من القرآن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the ba as accompaniment because that avoids implying God's name is an instrument; it may alternatively indicate seeking aid.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r6.anchor: وجوز كون الباء للأستعانة متعلقة بما عندها أو بمحذوف وقع حالا ورجحت الملابسة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r7.claim: The command is not impossible even if immediate: the Prophet knows that whatever is revealed as Quran is what he must read, so the command itself can be part of the material to read.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r7.anchor: ثم أنه ليس في الأمر المذكور تكليف بما لا يطاق سواء دل الأمر على الفور أم لا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r8.speaker: الآمدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r8.claim: Al-Amidi cites the repeated command Read followed by this passage as an example of clarification delayed until after the original command; al-Alusi accepts the passage as the clarification but rejects making the whole passage or basmala the object of the earlier command.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r8.anchor: قال الآمدي عند ذكر أدلة جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r9.claim: Calling God Lord and adding the possessive for Muhammad recalls divine nurturing and his gradual attainment of human perfection through recurring revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r9.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية المنبئة عن التربية والتبليغ إلى الكمال اللائق شيئا فشيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r10.claim: Who created recalls God's original favor and ability to teach reading; it may mean the one who creates or the one who created everything, and it rules out idols as true lords because Arabs did not ascribe creation to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178#2/r10.anchor: ووصف الرب بقوله تعالى الذي خلق لتذكيره عليه الصلاة والسلام أول النعماء الفائضة عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r3.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r3.claim: Al-Jubbai says the first Read commands personal reading or reading generally, while the second is reading for proclamation; another view connects the latter to prayer, and the Lord's generosity clause could be circumstantial or independent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r3.anchor: ولجبائي أن اقرأ الأول أمر بالقراءة لنفسه وقيل مطلقا والثاني أمر بالقراءة للتبليغ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says the clearest interpretation is that the second Read reinforces the first; the proposal to attach the basmala's باسم to the second command to make God's name the exclusive starting point is far-fetched because it normally attaches to the adjacent command.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r5.anchor: وأولى الأوجه وأظهرها التأكيد وأبعد بعضهم جدا فزعم أن بسم في البسملة متعلق باقرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r6.claim: The fronted command suits the importance of reading in the first surah revealed; even if another passage preceded it, the sense is read beginning with God's name, so other openings would not comply, while moving the name first changes the focus.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الظاهر تعلق باسم ربك بما عنده وتقديم الفعل ههنا أوقع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.claim: Most commentators say this was the first sura revealed and that its first five verses, through the words about what humanity did not know, were the first revelation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين: على أن هذه السورة أول سورة نزلت من القرآن، وأول ما نزل خمس آيات من أولها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.claim: Aisha says revelation began with true dreams and retreat to Hira; Gabriel commanded the Prophet to read and squeezed him three times before reciting these verses; he returned frightened and Khadija reassured him through his virtues.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.claim: Khadija brought the Prophet to Waraqa, who identified the visitor as the messenger sent to Moses, predicted his people would expel him, and promised support before dying as revelation paused.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.anchor: فانطلقت به خديجة حتى أتت به ورقة بن نوفل بن أسد بن عبد العزى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p478/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p478/r1.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p478/r1.claim: An expanded report says the Prophet became deeply distressed during the pause in revelation and repeatedly went to mountain peaks, where Gabriel reassured him that he was truly God's Messenger; the added account is marked as what reached the transmitters.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p478/r1.anchor: عن عائشة وذكر الحديث، قال: "اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق" حتى بلغ "ما لم يعلم" وزاد في آخره فقال: وفتر الوحي فترة حتى حزن النبي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p478/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p478/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p478/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda parses the phrase as read the name of your Lord, treating the preposition as extra; it means invoke God's name and begin reading with it as proper instruction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p478/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: مجازه: اقرأ اسم ربك، يعني أن الباء زائدة، والمعنى: اذكر اسمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r1.claim: The Creator first means all creatures, then the text specifies the human, meaning Adam's descendants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: يعني الخلائق، ثم فسره فقال: {خلق الإنسان} يعني

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r1.claim: The command is to recite the Qur'an beginning with God's name, or to recite seeking His aid.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r1.anchor: باسمه سبحانه وتعالى. أو مستعينا به.

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r2.claim: “Who created” can describe the One who owns creation or the One who created everything; the next verse then singles out humanity as the most remarkable creation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r2.anchor: أي الذي له الخلق أو الذي خلق كل شيء، ثم أفرد ما هو أشرف

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r4.claim: Since knowing God is the first obligation, the opening verses first show His existence, immense power, and complete wisdom.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r4.anchor: ولما كان أول الواجبات معرفة الله سبحانه وتعالى نزل أولا ما يدل على وجوده

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.claim: God recounts humanity's beginning and destination to show the favor of raising it from the lowest rank to the highest, affirm His lordship and generosity, and move from rational proof to sensory evidence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.anchor: وقد عدد سبحانه وتعالى مبدأ أمر الإنسان ومنتهاه إظهارا لما أنعم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r1.claim: The familiar name is Surat al-Alaq; al-Tabari calls it Surat Iqra or Iqra bi-smi rabbik, while al-Razi calls it Surat al-Qalam, a name easily confused with the following surah, which he calls Nun.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r1.anchor: المشهور في اسمها: "سورة العلق" ويذكرها بعض المفسرين، كالطبري باسم "سورة اقرأ"

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.claim: She presents the surah’s opening as the first revelation, noting that Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari report no disagreement about that account.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.anchor: والمشهور كذلك أنه أمل سورة نزلت من الوحي. ولم يشر "ابن إسحاق" في (السيرة النبوية) إلي خلاف

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.claim: Aisha recounts Muhammad’s true dreams, retreat to Hira, Gabriel’s command and three embraces, and the recitation of the opening five verses, which remained fixed in his heart; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.anchor: عن "السيدة عائشة أم المؤمنين" قالت: "كان أول ما ابتدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.claim: Aisha continues that Muhammad saw Gabriel in the sky, returned to Khadija, and was reassured because his character included kinship, truthfulness, trustworthiness, hospitality, and helping in adversity; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.anchor: فقالت: أبشر يا ابن عم واثبت، فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبداً، إنك لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r1.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r1.claim: After hearing Muhammad’s account, Waraqa identifies him as the prophet of this community and bearer of the revelation given to Moses, predicts rejection and persecution, and wishes he could support him; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r1.anchor: فقال: والذي نفسي بيده إنك لنبي هذه الأمة، ولقد جاءك الناموس الأكبر الذي جاء موسى

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r2.speaker: الزمخشري والفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r2.claim: An alternative view in al-Kashshaf and al-Razi’s commentary makes the Fatiha the first revealed surah, followed by al-Alaq.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r2.anchor: ولكن هناك قولاً - في الكشاف وتفسير الرازي - أن الفاتحة كانت أول سورة نزلت من الوحي

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.claim: Al-Razi also transmits that only al-Alaq’s first five verses came at the start; the remainder came after public opposition and were joined to the surah by God’s command.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.anchor: أن الذي نزل من السورة أول الوحي، آياتها الخمس الأولى

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.claim: Al-Bahr al-Muhit says the surah is Meccan and its opening was the first revelation at Hira, as established in Bukhari and elsewhere; it judges the claims that al-Muddaththir or the Fatiha came first unsound.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.anchor: وقول جابر: أول ما نزل المدثر، وقول أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل: أول ما نزل الفاتحة، لا يصح

BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.claim: The reports in al-Tabari and the Prophetic biography stop the first-revelation account at verse five, supporting the view that the opening alone was first revealed.
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.anchor: حيث يقف الحديث فيهما عن اول ما نزل من الوحي، عند الآية الخامسة

BINTSHATI:v2p15/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r2.claim: The opening command to recite is striking because it begins revelation to an unlettered Prophet among an unlettered, pagan Bedouin people, with the Book as his miracle.
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r2.anchor: أن تكون كلمة {اقْرَأْ} أول ما استهل به الوحي إلى النبي الأمي المبعوث في الأميين رسولاً منهم

BINTSHATI:v2p15/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r3.claim: Interpret the early surah through what its first hearers understood, rather than later additions to its meaning.
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r3.anchor: ونحتاج هنا في هذه السورة المبكرة من أول الوحي، إلى تمثل ما كان لها

BINTSHATI:v2p15/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r4.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r4.claim: Al-Tabari did not allegorize the command because its ordinary Arabic meaning, reciting from a written or unwritten text, was clear; Arabs knew rabb as owner and object of worship.
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r4.anchor: لم يجد حاجة إلى تأويل آية: {اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ} لوضوح معناها

BINTSHATI:v2p15/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r5.claim: The command is to recite in the name of the Creator, the rightful Lord rather than the idols the Arabs had fashioned and then worshiped.
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r5.anchor: فباسم ربه الذي خلق، أمر المصطفى أن يقرأ. وقد كان لقبائل العرب الوثنية أربابها من أوثان وأصنام

BINTSHATI:v2p16/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r1.claim: The surrounding religious scene was dark: northern Arabian Jews had forgotten Moses and worshiped gold, Syrian and Najrani Christians were divided, and Magians worshiped fire.
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r1.anchor: والنصارى - في الشام ونجران - قد مزقتهم التفرقة المذهبية، فبعضهم لبعض عدو

BINTSHATI:v2p16/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r2.claim: For the solitary seeker at Hira, the first revealed words guided him to the truth he sought and ended his long uncertainty like a new dawn.
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r2.anchor: توجيهاً وهداية إلى الحق الذيى طال التماسه إياه، وإذاناً بانتهاء حيرته

BINTSHATI:v2p16/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r3.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r3.claim: Al-Razi takes the command to recite in God’s name as implying that every Quran recitation should begin with God’s name.
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r3.anchor: في قوله: {اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ} إشعاراً بأن كل قراءة القرآن يجب أن تبدأ باسم الله

BINTSHATI:v2p16/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r4.claim: She hesitates over al-Razi’s distinction that rabb is an attribute of action whereas Allah is an essential name, with worship here commanded through the former.
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r4.anchor: أن الرب من صفات الفعل والله من أسماء الذات.... فالأمر هنا يستوجب العبادة بصفات الفعل

BINTSHATI:v2p16/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r5.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r5.claim: Al-Razi says Rabbika comforts the Prophet: God has nurtured him from an embryo into a knowing believer, so he should neither fear nor expect abandonment; the command also obliges him to act.
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r5.anchor: ما يزيل فزع الرسول من الوحي. فكأنه قال: ربك هو الذي رباك فكيف يفزعك

BINTSHATI:v2p16/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r6.claim: She centers Rabbika on the Prophet’s long search for guidance: the Creator revealed Himself as the Lord worthy of worship over created Arabian idols.
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r6.anchor: وهذا هو نور الكلمة يشرق فيهديه إلى ربه الذي خلق، الجدير بالعبادة دون هذه الأرباب المخلوقة

BINTSHATI:v2p16/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r7.claim: She rejects supplying an unstated object for خلق and keeps the first verse’s creation unqualified; the following verse then specifies the human being.
BINTSHATI:v2p16/r7.anchor: ولا وجه عندنا لما تعلق به بعض المفسرين من تأول مفعول لـ {خَلَقَ} في الآية الأولى

BINTSHATI:v2p17/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r1.claim: The first verse states creation generally, while the next specifies the human, recipient of revelation and the one uniquely able to read, learn, and bear religious responsibility.
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r1.anchor: تخصيص هذا العام، باللفت إلى خلق الإنسان، من حيث كان الوحي القرآني لهداية هذا الإنسان

BINTSHATI:v2p17/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r2.claim: Al-Razi transmits an argument that naming God as Creator leads idolaters gradually to acknowledge Him: they know they did not create themselves and that their handmade idols did not create them.
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r2.anchor: فقدم تعالى في {الَّذِي خَلَقَ} مقدمة تلجئهم إلى الاعتراف به

BINTSHATI:v2p17/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r3.claim: The context plainly asserts the Creator’s lordship; humans are singled out because they read, learn, bear obligations, and receive the revealed words.
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r3.anchor: وسياق الآيات صريح في أنه تقرير لربوبية الخالق. وتخصيص خلق الإنسان بالذكر دون سائر المخلوقات

BINTSHATI:v2p18/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan says Rabbuka comforts Muhammad and identifies his exclusive Lord; the Creator attribute follows because Arabs called idols lords, though idols cannot create.
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r1.anchor: ذكر {رَبَّكُ} في الآية الأولى، إيناس للمصطفى وتعيين لربه، لا رب غيره

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r1.claim: Some exegetes, as al-Razi transmits, say the first اقرأ is for the Prophet himself and the second for proclamation to others.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r1.anchor: أن {اقْرَأْ} في الآية الأولى تعني: "اقرأ لنفسك، وهي في هذه الآية بمعنى التبليغ

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r2.claim: A second reported interpretation makes the first command to read for learning and the second to teach.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r2.anchor: أو أن الأولى للتعلم، والثانية للتعليم

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r3.claim: A third reported interpretation says the first recitation is in prayer and the second outside prayer.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r3.anchor: أو أن الأولى: اقرأ في صلاتك، والثانية: اقرأ خارج صلاتك

BINTSHATI:v2p20/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r4.claim: She prefers the straightforward context: the command to recite is reiterated, and revelation specifies what the Prophet should read in his Lord’s name.
BINTSHATI:v2p20/r4.anchor: وهي أقوال متقاربة، وإن كان الأولى لأخذ السياق على ظاهره، بما يفيد من تأكيد الأمر الإلهي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r3.claim: The active verb is placed before its prepositional phrase because this is more forceful, especially in the first revelation, where the command to read is paramount.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r3.anchor: وقدم الفعل العامل في الجار والمجرور هنا لأنه أوقع في النفس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r4.claim: Omitting the object of “read” signals that the reading is the comprehensive Qur'an, containing every good; God alone enables the Prophet to read it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r4.anchor: فالمعنى : أوجد القراءة لما لا مقروء غيره , وهو القرآن الجامع لكل خير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r5.claim: “In the name of your Lord” means beginning with the basmala, seeking the benefactor's aid, or mentioning His name; in the last reading, the name stands for His exalted attributes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r5.anchor: حال كونك مفتتحا القراءة { باسم ربك } أي بأن تبسمل , أو مستعينا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r6.speaker: قالوا
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r6.claim: They say recitation is not complete without naming God; naming Him honors both the name and its bearer and all His attributes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r6.anchor: قالوا : وهذا يدل على أن القراءة لا تكون تامة غلا بالتسمية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r7.claim: The Lord's nurturing attribute, rather than the encompassing divine name, comforts the Prophet and recalls the favors recalled in al-Sharḥ; the command came when he loved retreat for worship in Ḥirāʾ.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r7.anchor: وتأنيسا له صلى الله عليه وسلم لكونه أول ما نزل حين حبب إليه الخلاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r9.claim: The order to read the Qur'an also alludes to seeking refuge from devils when reciting.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#2/r9.anchor: وأشار إلى الاستعاذة بالأمر بالقرآن لما أفهمه قوله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r1.claim: The cited commands to seek refuge and the protective veil apply against human and jinn devils when reading the Qur'an.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r2.claim: Creation is placed before command because it is visible, easier to understand, and a clear proof of existence, power, and wisdom; knowing God through His acts is the first obligation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r2.anchor: وبدأ بالخلق لأنه محسوس بالعين , فهو أعلق بالفهم , وأقرب إلى التصور

BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r3.claim: The unexpressed object of “created” makes the attribute comprehensive: everything that comes into existence is God's making and remains subject to His permission, prevention, harm, or benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r3.anchor: وحذف مفعوله إشارة إلى أنه له هذا الوصف وهو التقدير والإيجاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r1.claim: The challenge about denying judgment cannot literally accuse the Prophet, whom God has protected from denial; it addresses his community, as in the conditional warning elsewhere.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r1.anchor: وحكم هذا القبيل واضح في حق من تعدىة إليه الخطاب وقصد بالحقيقة به من أمته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r2.claim: The intended question asks what could make people hesitate about judgment after clear evidence, and whether a wise God would create differing human states in the best form without purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r2.anchor: أفيليق به وهو العليم الخبير أن يجعل اختلاف أحوالكم في الشكوك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r3.claim: The Qur'an is the healing, clarifying guide to humanity's beginning and end, so the command is to read it reflectively; its description as guidance and mercy reinforces this role.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r3.anchor: وهو كتابه المبين , الذي جعله الله تعالى تبيانا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r4.claim: Humanity was created in the best form and then reduced to the lowest, producing opposing outcomes by God's prior wisdom and will; He could have guided every soul if He willed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r4.anchor: وأيضا فإنه تعالى أعلم عباده بخلقه الإنسان في أحسن تقويم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r5.claim: The preceding surahs show the highest outcome for the noblest human, the Prophet, including God's promise that He will give him until he is content.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p480/r5.anchor: حال نبينا المصطفى صلى الله عليه وسلم وجليل وعده الكريم له في قوله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p481/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p481/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p481/r3.claim: Repeating “Read” emphasizes the command, comforts the Prophet, and distinguishes the One who brings revelation from the false objects of worship; the Prophet had said he could not read.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p481/r3.anchor: مكررا للأمر بالقراءة تنبيها على عظم شأنها وتأنيسا له صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.claim: The author classifies the chapter as Meccan and counts nineteen verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r2.claim: He says the first Qur'an revelation in Mecca was ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created.’
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما نزل من القرآن بمكة {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق}

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r3.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r3.claim: He says ‘Read in the name of your Lord’ was the first sura revealed to Muhammad; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r3.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: كانت {اقرأ باسم ربك} أول سورة أنزلت على محمد

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r4.speaker: ابن شهاب
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r4.claim: Scholars he cites say the opening through ‘what he did not know’ was revealed at Hira and the rest came later.
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r4.anchor: عن ابن شهاب: حدثني محمد بن عباد بن جعفر المخزومي أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r5.claim: Aisha says the first revelation was ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created.’
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r5.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أول ما نزل من القرآن {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق}

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.claim: Aisha's account describes true dreams and retreat at Hira before Gabriel commands him to read, presses him three times, and recites the first five verses; Muhammad returns trembling to Khadija.
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم

DURR-FULL:v8p561/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r1.speaker: خديجة
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r1.claim: Khadija reassures the frightened Prophet that God will never disgrace him because he maintains kinship, bears burdens, helps the destitute, hosts guests, and supports just causes.
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r1.anchor: فقالت خديجة: كلا والله ما يخزيك الله أبدا إنك لتصل الرحم وتحمل الكل

DURR-FULL:v8p561/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r2.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r2.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the same Namus sent to Moses, predicts the Prophet's people will expel him, and promises support if he lives to that day.
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r2.anchor: فقال له ورقة: هذا الناموس الذي أنزل الله على موسى يا ليتني أكون فيها جذعا

DURR-FULL:v8p561/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r3.claim: After Waraqa's death and a pause in revelation, the Prophet sees the Hira angel seated between heaven and earth and retreats in fear.
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r3.anchor: أن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري قال وهو يحدث عن فترة الوحي فقال في حديثه: بينا أنا أمشي إذ

DURR-FULL:v8p561/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r5.claim: He says ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created’ was the first sura revealed to Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول سورة نزلت على محمد {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق}

DURR-FULL:v8p561/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r6.claim: He says the first revelation was ‘Read in the name of your Lord,’ followed by Nun and the Pen.
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: أول ما نزل من القرآن {اقرأ باسم ربك} ثم (ن والقلم)

DURR-FULL:v8p561/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r7.claim: He identifies the first thing revealed as five verses, from ‘Read in the name of your Lord’ through ‘what he did not know.’
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول شيء أنزل من القرآن خمس آيات {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق} إلى قوله: {ما لم يعلم}

DURR-FULL:v8p561/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r8.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r8.claim: He says ‘Read in the name of your Lord’ came first, followed by Nun.
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r8.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير قال: أول ما نزل من القرآن {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق} ثم (ن)

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r1.claim: Aisha reports that after ‘Read in the name of your Lord,’ revelations included Nun and the Pen, al-Muddaththir, and al-Duha.
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان أول ما نزل عليه بعد {اقرأ باسم ربك} {ن والقلم} و (يا أيها المدثر)

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r2.speaker: الزهري وعمرو بن دينار
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r2.claim: They report that at Hira an angel brought a brocade cloth inscribed with the first revelation through ‘what he did not know.’
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r2.anchor: عن الزهري وعمرو بن دينار أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذا أتاه ملك بنمط من ديباج

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r3.speaker: عمرو بن جابر
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r3.claim: He transmits the same report of an angel at Hira bringing the opening passage written on brocade.
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r3.anchor: من طريق عمرو بن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذا أتاه ملك بنمط من ديباج

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r4.claim: His account says Gabriel pressed Muhammad, recited the opening through ‘what he did not know,’ and later revelation paused; the descent of al-Duha answered Khadija's worry that God had abandoned him.
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد قال: أتى جبريل محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا محمد اقرأ

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r5.claim: Aisha relates the Prophet's retreat with Khadija, encounter with Gabriel and Michael, opening of his belly and chest, then command to read; he retained the verses thereafter.
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r5.anchor: عن عائشة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعتكف هو وخديجة شهرا فوافق ذلك رمضان

DURR-FULL:v8p563/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r1.speaker: ميكائيل
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r1.claim: In the continuing report, Gabriel weighs the Prophet against one, then two, then one hundred men; Michael says his community will follow him, and stones and trees greet him as God's Messenger.
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r1.anchor: ثم وزنني جبريل برجل فوازنته ثم وزنني بأخر فوازنته ثم وزنني بمائة فقال ميكائيل: تبعته أمته

DURR-FULL:v8p563/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r2.claim: Thawban's report says Umar heard his sister reciting the opening passage, came to Muhammad, and accepted Islam after the Prophet invited him to testify to God's oneness and Muhammad's messengership.
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r2.anchor: عن ثوبان قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم أعز الإسلام بعمر بن الخطاب

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says in al-Umm that, although it is said refuge is sought in every rakʿa, his own position is to seek refuge only in the first rakʿa.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r1.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه في الأم

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r2.claim: A defense of Al-Shāfiʿī’s first-rakʿa-only position appeals to the default absence of obligation and says the conditional إذا in the command to seek refuge when reciting does not itself mean every time.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r2.anchor: بأن الأصل هو العدم وما لأجله أمرنا بذكر الاستعاذة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r3.claim: The counterargument is that when a ruling is attached to a relevant description, that description indicates its cause, so the ruling recurs whenever its cause recurs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r3.anchor: ترتيب الحكم على الوصف المناسب يدل على العلية فيلزم أن يتكرر الحكم بتكرر العلة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r4.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa require the formula seeking refuge in God from accursed Satan, matching the wording of the Qur’anic command and the apparent wording of a report from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r4.anchor: فقال الشافعي : واجب أن يقول : أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم وهو قول أبي حنيفة

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r5.speaker: أحمد
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r5.claim: Aḥmad considers it preferable to add إنه هو السميع العليم to the standard formula, thereby combining the two cited Qur’anic wordings.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r5.anchor: أحمد : الأولى أن يقول أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r6.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r6.claim: Some of al-Rāzī’s companions prefer placing السميع العليم after بالله and before من الشيطان الرجيم, also combining the two verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r6.anchor: وقال بعض أصحابنا الأولى أن يقول

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r7.claim: Al-Bayhaqī reports from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that when the Prophet rose at night, he said takbīr three times and sought refuge in God, the All-Hearing, All-Knowing, from Satan.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r8.speaker: الثوري والأوزاعي
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r8.claim: Al-Thawrī and al-Awzāʿī prefer adding إن الله هو السميع العليم after the standard refuge formula.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r8.anchor: وقال الثوري والأوزاعي : الأولى أن يقول

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that Gabriel first instructed Muḥammad to seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, All-Knowing, from Satan, then instructed him to recite the basmala and the opening of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq; al-Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r9.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس أن أول ما نزل جبريل على محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r10.claim: Seeking refuge purifies the heart of what blocks absorption in God, while the basmala turns the heart toward the awe of God’s majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p59/r10.anchor: فالاستعاذة تطهر القلب عن كل ما يكون مانعا من الاستغراق في الله والتسمية توجه القلب إلى هيبة جلال الله

TAB:96:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:1/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:1/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad to recite in remembrance of his Lord, the Creator.
TAB:96:1/r1.anchor: اقرأ يا محمد بذكر ربك الذي خلق

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r1.claim: Some authorities said the first revelation was 'Read in the name of your Lord.'
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r1.anchor: فمنهم من قال قوله ( ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ )

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r2.claim: Others said the first revelation was 'O you wrapped up.'
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r2.anchor: ومنهم من قال ( ﴿ يا أيها المدثر ﴾ )

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r3.claim: A further view named the Opening of the Book as the first revelation.

BURHAN:v3p235/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p235/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p235/r3.claim: Two explanations are offered for placing the verb before “in the name of your Lord”: the act is foremost because this was the first revealed sūrah, or the phrase attaches to the second “recite.”
BURHAN:v3p235/r3.anchor: وأجيب بوجهين أحدهما أن تقديم الفعل هناك أهم لأنها أول سورة نزلت

BURHAN:v1p390/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.speaker: علماء الظاهر
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.claim: The outward scholars explain the omission as abbreviation from frequent use: the alif of ism is dropped only when appended to Allah and preceded by ba according to the majority.
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.anchor: وعلماء الظاهر يقولون للاختصار وكثرة الاستعمال وهو من خصائص الجلالة الشريفة

BURHAN:v1p65/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p65/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p65/r2.claim: The extra endings الأعلى in al-Aʿla and خلق in al-ʿAlaq suit each surah’s cadence, matching the surrounding verse endings.
BURHAN:v1p65/r2.anchor: فزاد فى الأولى ﴿ الأعلى ﴾ وزاد فى الثانية ﴿ خلق ﴾ مراعاة للفواصل فى السورتين

BURHAN:v2p470/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p470/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p470/r2.claim: The command first states that God created generally, then singles out the human being's creation from a clot.
BURHAN:v2p470/r2.anchor: وقوله ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق ﴾ فعم بقوله ﴿ خلق ﴾ جميع مخلوقاته ثم خص فقال

BURHAN:v1p180/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p180/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p180/r1.claim: The seventh type of sūra opening begins with a command and occurs in six sūras: “Say, it was revealed,” “Read,” and four further “Say” or “I seek refuge” openings.
BURHAN:v1p180/r1.anchor: االسابع الاستفتااح بالأمر فى ست سور

BURHAN:v4p251/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p251/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p251/r7.claim: باء also appears with objects in examples such as بأيديكم, بالمودة, باسم ربك, and بأيكم المفتون; المفتون is a passive participle, not a verbal noun.
BURHAN:v4p251/r7.anchor: وإما مع المفعول كقوله تعالى ﴿ ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة ﴾ وقوله ﴿ تلقون إليهم بالمودة ﴾

BURHAN:v1p207/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p207/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p207/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says the best-supported view is that the first revealed verses were اقرأ باسم ربك, with يا أيها المدثر next in strength.
BURHAN:v1p207/r3.anchor: وأثبت الأقاويل ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ ويليه فى القوة ﴿ يا أيها المدثر ﴾

BURHAN:v1p207/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p207/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p207/r4.claim: The views can be reconciled: اقرأ was the first verses, المدثر the first preaching commands, and al-Fātiḥa the first complete sūra revealed.
BURHAN:v1p207/r4.anchor: أن أول ما نزل من الآيات ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ وأول ما نزل من أوامر التبليغ ﴿ يا أيها المدثر ﴾

BURHAN:v1p207/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p207/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p207/r5.claim: The distinction resembles reports that prayer is the first duty reckoned and bloodshed the first dispute judged: each is first within a different category.
BURHAN:v1p207/r5.anchor: وهذا كما ورد فى الحديث أول ما يحاسب به العبد الصلاة وأول ما يقضى فيه الدماء

BURHAN:v1p207/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p207/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p207/r6.claim: Another distinction says اقرأ باسم ربك was first for prophethood, while يا أيها المدثر was first for messengership, since the latter commands a general public warning.
BURHAN:v1p207/r6.anchor: وقيل أول ما نزل للرسالة ﴿ يا أيها المدثر ﴾ وللنبوة ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾

BURHAN:v1p207/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p207/r8.speaker: مجاهد
BURHAN:v1p207/r8.claim: Mujāhid says the first sūra revealed was اقرأ, followed by Nūḥ.
BURHAN:v1p207/r8.anchor: وعن مجاهد قال أول سورة أنزلت اقرأ ثم نوح

BURHAN:v2p486/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p486/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
BURHAN:v2p486/r4.claim: The anonymous poetic lines repeat النوى, separation, and al-Aṣmaʿī jokes that the second version deserved a she-goat, illustrating the effect of repeated wording.
BURHAN:v2p486/r4.anchor: وسمع الأصمعي من ينشد … فما للنوى جد النوى قطع النوى … كذاك النوى قطاعه للقرائن

BURHAN:v2p486/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p486/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p486/r6.claim: Poetic repetition of حديث and the beloved's dwelling shows how repeating a subject can delight the listener.
BURHAN:v2p486/r6.anchor: كرّر على السمع منى أيها الحادي … ذكر المنازل والأطلال والنادي

ITQAN:v3p284/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.claim: The opening of “Read” similarly previews the Qur’an: it commands reading, begins in God’s name, signals legal knowledge and the principles of religion, and reports God’s teaching of what humans did not know; it can therefore be called the Qur’an’s title.
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.anchor: وكذلك أول سورة ( اقرأ فإنها مشتملة على نظير ما اشتملت عليه الفاتحة من براعة الاستهلال

ITQAN:v1p76/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p76/r1.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p76/r1.claim: Ibn Hajar distinguishes the first revelation prompted by an earlier event—the Prophet's fright and covering himself—from “Read,” which was revealed initially without a prior cause.
ITQAN:v1p76/r1.anchor: رابعها أن المراد أول ما نزل بسبب متقدم وهو ما وقع من التدثر الناشئ عن الرعب وأما

ITQAN:v1p76/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p76/r2.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v1p76/r2.claim: Al-Kirmani argues that Jabir inferred his view rather than narrating it, so Aisha's transmitted report should take precedence.
ITQAN:v1p76/r2.anchor: أن جابرا استخرج ذلك باجتهاده وليس هو من روايته فيقدم عليه ما روته عائشة قاله الكرماني

ITQAN:v1p76/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p76/r7.speaker: عكرمة والحسن
ITQAN:v1p76/r7.claim: Ibn al-Naqib mentions a fourth view that the basmala was first revealed; a report from Ikrima and al-Hasan says it was first, while the first sura was “Read.”
ITQAN:v1p76/r7.anchor: وأخرج الواحدي بإسناده عن عكرمة والحسن قالا أول ما نزل من القرآن

ITQAN:v3p283/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p283/r2.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v3p283/r2.claim: Abu Shama counts six sūras that open with a command, including those beginning qul, iqraʾ, and sabbiḥ.
ITQAN:v3p283/r2.anchor: السابع الأمر في ست سور قل أوحي اقرأ قل يا أيها الكافرون قل هو الله أحد قل أعوذ المعوذتين

ITQAN:v3p298/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p298/r7.speaker: الخطابي
ITQAN:v3p298/r7.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī says the Companions placed al-Qadr after al-ʿAlaq, inferring that the pronoun in 'We sent it down' refers to the command 'Read'; Ibn al-ʿArabī calls the inference remarkable.
ITQAN:v3p298/r7.anchor: حكى الخطابي أن الصحابة لما اجتمعوا على القرآن وضعوا سورة القدر عقب العلق استدلوا بذلك

ITQAN:v1p74/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p74/r1.claim: Of the reports about the first revelation, the soundest view is that it began with اقرأ باسم ربك; Aisha’s report in the two Sahih collections recounts the true dreams, retreat at Hira, and Gabriel’s three commands to read through ما لم يعلم.
ITQAN:v1p74/r1.anchor: أحدها وهو الصحيح ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾

ITQAN:v1p74/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p74/r2.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v1p74/r2.claim: Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi authenticate Aisha’s report that اقرأ باسم ربك was the first surah revealed.
ITQAN:v1p74/r2.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم في المستدرك والبيهقي في الدلائل وصححاه عن عائشة قالت أول سورة نزلت

ITQAN:v1p74/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p74/r3.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
ITQAN:v1p74/r3.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits with a chain meeting the soundness standard Abu Raja’s report that Abu Musa called this the first surah sent to Muhammad.
ITQAN:v1p74/r3.anchor: أخرج الطبراني في الكبير بسند على شرط الصحيح عن أبي رجاء العطاردي قال كان أبو موسى يقرئنا

ITQAN:v1p74/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p74/r4.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ITQAN:v1p74/r4.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr reports that Gabriel instructed the Prophet to read and then recited اقرأ باسم ربك, which the Prophet called the first revelation.
ITQAN:v1p74/r4.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير قال جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له اقرأ

ITQAN:v1p74/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p74/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v1p74/r5.claim: Mujahid says the first revelation included both اقرأ باسم ربك and ن والقلم, an alternative to the preferred report that begins with اقرأ.
ITQAN:v1p74/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال إن أول ما أنزل من القرآن ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ و ﴿ ن والقلم ﴾

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r5.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r5.claim: Ibn Hisham notes that the first five verses of al-ʿAlaq were the earliest revelation, then kallā opened a new statement, which challenges the rebuke-only reading.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r5.anchor: وأيضا فإن أول ما نزل خمس آيات من أول سورة العلق ثم نزل ﴿ كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى ﴾ فجاءت في افتتاح الكلام

ITQAN:v1p120/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p120/r1.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v1p120/r1.claim: Abu Shāma says the Qur’an’s descent all at once to the lowest heaven apparently preceded prophethood, though it may have occurred afterward.
ITQAN:v1p120/r1.anchor: قال أبو شامة أيضا الظاهر أن نزوله جملة إلى السماء الدنيا قبل ظهور نبوته صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ويحتمل أن يكون بعدها

ITQAN:v1p120/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p120/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti favors the second possibility, descent after prophethood, because the preceding reports from Ibn Abbas state this explicitly.
ITQAN:v1p120/r2.anchor: قلت الظاهر هو الثاني وسياق الآثار السابقة عن ابن عباس صريح فيه

ITQAN:v1p120/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p120/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p120/r3.claim: Wathila reports the Prophet said the Torah descended on 6 Ramadan, the Gospel on 13, the Psalms on 18, and the Qur’an on 24; another wording places Abraham’s scrolls on the first night.
ITQAN:v1p120/r3.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أنزلت التوراة لست مضين من رمضان والإنجيل لثلاث عشرة خلت منه والزبور لثمان عشرة

ITQAN:v1p120/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p120/r4.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p120/r4.claim: Ibn Hajar links the 24 Ramadan report to verses about Ramadan and Laylat al-Qadr, proposing a whole descent to the lowest heaven then and the first earthly revelation on the 24th.
ITQAN:v1p120/r4.anchor: وهذا الحديث مطابق لقوله تعالى ﴿ شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن ﴾ ولقوله ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ﴾

ITQAN:v1p120/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p120/r5.speaker: البيهقي وغيره
ITQAN:v1p120/r5.claim: To reconcile the famous claim that the Prophet was sent in Rabi, a report says he first received prophetic dreams in his birth month for six months, then revelation while awake.
ITQAN:v1p120/r5.anchor: ويجاب عن هذا بما ذكروه أنه نبئ أولا بالرؤيا في شهر مولده ثم كانت مدتها ستة أشهر ثم أوحي إليه في اليقظة ذكره البيهقي وغيره

ITQAN:v1p120/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p120/r6.speaker: أبو قلابة
ITQAN:v1p120/r6.claim: Abu Qilaba’s report that all scriptures descended complete on the night of 24 Ramadan complicates the preceding date account.
ITQAN:v1p120/r6.anchor: يشكل على الحديث السابق ما أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة في فضائل القرآن عن أبي قلابة قال أنزلت الكتب كاملة ليلة أربع وعشرين من رمضان

ITQAN:v1p120/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p120/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p120/r7.claim: Answering why the Qur’an was not sent all at once, al-Suyuti says God sent it gradually to strengthen the Prophet’s heart, as 25:32 states.
ITQAN:v1p120/r7.anchor: فأجابهم تعالى بقوله ﴿ كذلك ﴾ أي أنزلناه كذلك مفرقا ﴿ لنثبت به فؤادك ﴾ أي لنقوي به قلبك

ITQAN:v1p120/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p120/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p120/r8.claim: Fresh revelation with each event strengthens the Prophet and renews divine care and angelic contact, bringing joy; this is why he was most generous in Ramadan, when he often met Gabriel.
ITQAN:v1p120/r8.anchor: فإن الوحي إذا كان يتجدد في كل حادثة كان أقوى بالقلب وأشد عناية بالمرسل إليه

ITQAN:v1p292#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r1.claim: Prostration is recommended when reciting a prostration verse; the fourteen are in al-Araf, al-Rad, al-Nahl, al-Isra, Maryam, twice in al-Hajj, al-Furqan, al-Naml, al-Sajda, Fussilat, al-Najm, al-Inshiqaq, and al-Alaq.
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r1.anchor: يسن السجود عند قراءة آية السجدة وهي أربع عشرة في الأعراف والرعد والنحل والإسراء ومريم وفي الحج سجدتان

ITQAN:v1p292#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r2.claim: The prostration in Sad is recommended but not among the emphatic prostrations.
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r2.anchor: وأما ص فمستحبة وليست من عزائم السجود أي متأكداته

ITQAN:v1p292#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r3.claim: Some scholars add a prostration at the end of al-Hijr; Ibn al-Faris transmits this in his Ahkam.
ITQAN:v1p292#2/r3.anchor: وزاد بعضهم آخر الحجر نقله ابن الفرس في أحكامه

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says revelation began with true dreams and seclusion at Ḥirāʾ; Gabriel's repeated commands to recite introduced al-ʿAlaq, and the shaken Prophet was comforted by Khadīja, who cited his virtues. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت: "أول ما بدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r2.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r2.claim: A further report from ʿĀʾisha identifies “Read in the name of your Lord who created” as the Quran's first revelation; al-Ḥākim includes it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r2.anchor: عن عروة، عن عائشة قالت: إن أول ما نزل من القرآن {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق}

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r1.speaker: عكرمة والحسن
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r1.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḥasan say the basmala was the first revelation in Mecca and the opening of Sūrat Iqra.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة والحسن قالا: أول ما نزل من القرآن {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم}

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.speaker: بعض علمائهم
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.claim: Ibn Shihāb relays from Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād that some scholars said al-ʿAlaq's first five verses were revealed at Ḥirāʾ; the remainder came later as God willed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.anchor: أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول: كان أول ما أنزل الله على رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r1.claim: The author presents the work as a concise book on Qurʾānic parsing and meanings and asks God for success in all matters.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r1.anchor: هذا كتاب مختصر في إعراب القرآن ومعانيه، ونسأل الله التوفيق في كل الأمور

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r2.claim: The bāʾ supplies the sense of beginning: “I began in the name of God”; the verb “I began” is omitted because the situation makes it clear.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r2.anchor: الجالب للباء معنى الابتداء، كأنك قلت: بدأت باسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r3.claim: The first alif in ism is hamzat waṣl, used to pronounce an initial consonant cluster; it disappears phonetically, as shown by the diminutive and forms ism and sim.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r3.anchor: وسقطت الألف من باسم الله في اللفظ وكان الأصل

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r4.claim: The diminutive samī and Arab forms ism and sim, together with a rajaz line using simah, support the hamzat-waṣl analysis.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r4.anchor: قال الراجز: باسم الذي في كل سورة سمه.

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r5.claim: Ism derives from sumū, “elevation”; its original form is sumw, and its plural asmāʾ follows patterns such as qanū/aqnāʾ and ḥanū/aḥnāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r5.anchor: ومعنى قولنا اسم: إنه مشتق من السمو، والسمو الرفعة

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r6.claim: A name draws attention to God's name through its meaning, since the meaning lies beneath the name.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r6.anchor: وإنما جعل الاسم تنويها باسم الله على المعنى؛ لأن المعنى تحت الإسم

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r7.claim: He rejects derivation from wasama, “to mark”: it would require a root-initial wāw to disappear after hamzat waṣl, unlike the patterns of ʿidda and zina.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r7.anchor: ومن قال: إن اسما مأخوذ من " وسمت " فهو غلط

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r8.claim: If ism came from wasama, its diminutive should be wasīm, like waʿīda and waṣīla from words whose root-initial wāw is dropped; this is not the case.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r8.anchor: فلو كان " اسم " وسمة لكان تصغيره إذا حذفت منه ألف الوصل " وسيم "

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r9.claim: Writing omits the alif in bism Allāh but retains it in bi-smi rabbika; omission in the basmala reflects its spoken elision and frequent use.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r9.anchor: وسقطت الألف في الكتاب من " بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم "

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r10.speaker: سِيبَوَيْهِ
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r10.claim: Sībawayh says bāʾ means attachment: writing with a pen means the writing is attached to the pen.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r10.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن معنى الباء الإلصاق، تقول كتبت بالقلم والمعنى أن الكتابة ملصقة بالقلم

ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r11.claim: The preposition bi is always kasra because it governs genitive; its vowel distinguishes the particle bi-Zayd from the noun kā-Zayd, which also governs genitive.
ZAJJAJ:v1p39/r11.anchor: وهي مكسورة أبدا لأنه - لا معنى لها إلا الخفض

NASHR:v1p247/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p247/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p247/r1.claim: The command istaʿidh asks for refuge; saying aʿūdhu performs that refuge, whereas astaʿīdhu only says that one is seeking to take refuge.
NASHR:v1p247/r1.anchor: فمعنى استعذت بالله أطلب منه أن يعيذك

NASHR:v1p247/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p247/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p247/r2.claim: The formula astaghfiru Allāh appropriately remains a request, because forgiveness can only be granted by God, unlike refuge which the speaker takes by turning to Him.
NASHR:v1p247/r2.anchor: أنه يطلب المغفرة التي لا تتأتى إلا منه بخلاف العياذ

NASHR:v1p247/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p247/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
NASHR:v1p247/r3.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās says Gabriel first told Muhammad to seek refuge; he replied with a formula seeking refuge in the All-Hearing, All-Knowing, then came the basmalah and the command to read.
NASHR:v1p247/r3.anchor: عبد الله بن عباس قال: أول ما نزل جبريل

NASHR:v1p247/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p247/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v1p247/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr calls the Ibn ʿAbbās report unusual and says its chain is weak and disconnected, so it cannot serve as proof.
NASHR:v1p247/r4.anchor: أبو الفداء إسماعيل بن كثير - رحمه الله - بعد إيراده: وهذا إسناد غريب

NASHR:v1p247/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p247/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p247/r5.claim: Al-Dānī gives what the author calls the correct version from Abū Rūq through al-Ḍaḥḥāk to Ibn ʿAbbās, saying Gabriel first taught the Prophet; the excerpt ends before the account is completed.
NASHR:v1p247/r5.anchor: فإن الحافظ أبا عمرو الداني - رحمه الله تعالى - رواه على الصواب من حديث أبي روق

IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.speaker: عبيد
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.claim: Ubayd's report says Muhammad annually secluded himself at Hira during Ramadan, fed the poor, and returned to circumambulate the Kaaba; Gabriel then came with a written silk cloth and commanded him to recite, repeating the embrace three times, after which Muhammad woke with the words fixed in his heart.
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.anchor: قال عبيد: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجاور ذلك الشهر من كل سنة، يطعم من جاءه من المساكين

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r1.claim: Sura al-ʿAlaq is Meccan, and its opening was the first revelation, sent down in the cave of Hira according to reports established in Sahih al-Bukhari and other sources.
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية ، وصدرها أول ما نزل من القرآن ، وذلك في غار حراء على ما ثبت في صحيح البخاري وغيره

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r2.speaker: جابر
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r2.claim: Jabir gives a contrary report that the first revelation was al-Muddaththir.
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r2.anchor: وقول جابر : أول ما نزل المدثر

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r3.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r3.claim: Abu Maysara ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil said al-Fatiha was first revealed, but Abū Ḥayyān judges this report unsound.
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r3.anchor: وقول أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل : أول ما نزل الفاتحة لا يصح

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r4.speaker: الزمخشري عن ابن عباس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari, reporting Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid, says this was the first sura revealed.
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري ، عن ابن عباس ومجاهد : هي أول سورة نزلت

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r5.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says most exegetes hold that al-Fatiha was first revealed, followed by al-Qalam.
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r5.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة القلم

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r6.claim: Following the preceding mention of human creation in the best formation and what later happened to humanity, this sura recalls human stages and God's favor, then its transgression and its afterlife outcome.
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r6.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها خلق الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ، ثم ذكر ما عرض له بعد ذلك ، ذكره هنا منبهاً على شيء من أطواره

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r7.claim: The majority pronounce اقرأ with a quiescent hamza.

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r8.speaker: الأعشى عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r8.claim: Al-Aʿsha, through Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, drops the hamza; Abū Ḥayyān explains it as a form like قرأ يقرأ, yielding an imperative like اسع.
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r8.anchor: والأعشى ، عن أبي بكر ، عن عاصم : بحذفها ، كأنه على قول من يبدل الهمزة بمناسب حركتها

ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r9.claim: The preposition is apparently attached to اقرأ as an instrumental phrase, while its object is omitted: read what is revealed to you.
ABUHAYYAN:96:1/r9.anchor: والظاهر تعلق الباء باقرأ وتكون للاستعانة ، ومفعول اقرأ محذوف ، أي اقرأ ما يوحى إليك
