IBNKATHIR:96:5/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr says these opening verses are God's first mercy to humanity and His first blessing upon them.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r7.anchor: وهُنَّ أول رحمة رَحم الله بها العباد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r1.claim: Anas reports that God kept sending revelation to the Messenger, with its greatest frequency, until shortly before his death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r1.anchor: أخبرني أنس بن مالك أن الله تابع الوحي على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل وفاته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that revelation came gradually whenever needed; after the initial pause following the angel’s first descent, it did not lapse again and then came in a steady succession.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r2.anchor: ومعناه: أن الله تعالى تابع نزول الوحي على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا بعد شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r3.claim: The first revelation was the command ‘Read in the name of your Lord’; the following hiatus lasted about two years or more, and the first revelation after it was the command to rise and warn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r3.anchor: بعد نزول الملك أول مرة بقوله: {اقرأ باسم ربك} [العلق: 1] فإنه استلبث الوحي بعدها حينا يقال: قريبا من سنتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r4.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله البجلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r4.claim: Jundab reports that after the Prophet was ill for a night or two, a woman said his Satan had abandoned him, and Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā was revealed in response; Ibn Kathir notes its transmission by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasaʾi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r4.anchor: سمعت جندبا يقول: اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين، فأتته امرأة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that these reports belong in a discussion of Qur’an’s virtues because they show God’s great care and love for the Messenger: revelation was not cut off, and the Qur’an came piecemeal as an honor to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p22/r5.anchor: والمناسبة في ذكر هذا الحديث والذي قبله في فضائل القرآن: أن الله تعالى له برسوله عناية عظيمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r1.speaker: القاضي الباقلاني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r1.claim: Al-Baqillani reports that his codex began with ‘Read in the name of your Lord, the Most Generous’; Ibn Masʿud’s began with al-Fatiha’s ‘Master of the Day of Judgment,’ while Ubayy’s began with al-Fatiha and then placed surahs in a different order.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r1.anchor: حكى القاضي الباقلاني: أن أول مصحفه كان: "اقرأ باسم ربك الأكرم" وأول مصحف ابن مسعود: {مالك يوم الدين}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r2.speaker: القاضي الباقلاني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r2.claim: Al-Baqillani considers it possible that Companions exercised judgment in arranging the surahs in today’s codex; Makki says the order of verses and the opening basmalas came from the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r2.anchor: ثم قال القاضي: ويحتمل أن ترتيب السور في المصحف على ما هو عليه اليوم من اجتهاد الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r3.speaker: ربيعة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r3.claim: Asked why al-Baqara and Aal ʿImran lead despite more than eighty surahs preceding them in revelation, Rabiʿa answers that knowledgeable compilers arranged the Qur’an by consensus, so the matter is not open to questioning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r3.anchor: سمعت سليمان بن بلال يقول: سئل ربيعة: لم قدمت البقرة وآل عمران، وقد نزل قبلهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r4.claim: Malik says the Qur’an’s arrangement follows what the Companions heard from the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r4.anchor: وسمعت مالكا يقول: إنما ألف القرآن على ما كانوا يسمعونه من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن بن بطال
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r5.claim: Ibn Battal says surah order in the written codex is not binding in prayer, recitation, or study; he cites Aisha’s statement that whichever surah one reads first is harmless and the Prophet’s use of nonconsecutive surahs in successive prayer units.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r5.anchor: قال أبو الحسن بن بطال: إنا نجد (5) تأليف سوره في الرسم والخط خاصة ولا يعلم أن أحدا منهم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r6.claim: Ibn Battal explains that Ibn Masʿud and Ibn Umar’s censure of reading the Qur’an backwards means reversing a surah from end to beginning; that practice is forbidden, not merely reading surahs out of codex order.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r6.anchor: وأما ما روي عن ابن مسعود وابن عمر أنهما كرها أن يقرأ القرآن منكوسا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud describes al-Israʾ, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ta Ha, and the Prophets as among the ancient early surahs and among his old, long-held possessions; al-Bukhari alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r7.anchor: سمعت ابن مسعود يقول في بني إسرائيل والكهف ومريم وطه والأنبياء: إنهن من العتاق الأول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir glosses ‘the ancient ones’ as early revelation and ‘my talad’ as old possessions or memorized material; talid means old wealth or goods, contrasted with tarif, the new.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p48/r8.anchor: والمراد منه ذكر ترتيب هذه السور في مصحف ابن مسعود كالمصاحف العثمانية، وقوله: "من العتاق الأول" أي: من قديم ما نزل

MUSNAD-AHMAD:25959/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25959/r1.speaker: عائشة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25959/r1.claim: Aisha reports clear dreams preceded Muhammad’s worship at Hira; Gabriel’s three squeezes led to reciting al-ʿAlaq 96:1–5. Khadija consoled him citing virtues; Waraqa identified Gabriel as Moses’s messenger and predicted opposition; after a reported pause, Gabriel reassured him.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25959/r1.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت: " أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:96:1/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:1/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:1/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has nineteen verses.

KASHSHAF:96:1/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:1/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
KASHSHAF:96:1/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid say this was the first sūra revealed.
KASHSHAF:96:1/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد : هي أول سورة نزلت

KASHSHAF:96:1/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:1/r3.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
KASHSHAF:96:1/r3.claim: Most commentators hold that al-Fātiḥa was revealed first, followed by Sūrat al-Qalam.
KASHSHAF:96:1/r3.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة القلم

KASHSHAF:96:1/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:1/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:1/r4.claim: Bi-smi rabbika is an accusative circumstantial phrase: read beginning with the name of your Lord, saying “In the name of God,” then read.
KASHSHAF:96:1/r4.anchor: النصب على الحال ،   أي : اقرأ مفتتحاً باسم ربك

KASHSHAF:96:1/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:1/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:1/r5.claim: One analysis leaves khalaqa without an understood object: God alone brought creation into being and there is no other creator.
KASHSHAF:96:1/r5.anchor: إما أن لا يقدر له مفعول وأن يراد أنه الذي حصل منه الخلق واستأثر به لا خالق سواه

KASHSHAF:96:1/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:1/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:1/r6.claim: Alternatively, its unexpressed object is “everything”: the word is unrestricted, so no subset of created things is more deserving of being supplied.
KASHSHAF:96:1/r6.anchor: وإما أن يقدر ويراد خلق كل شيء ،   فيتناول كل مخلوق

MAWARDI:96:1/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:1/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:1/r1.claim: Sūrat al-ʿAlaq is Meccan by consensus.
MAWARDI:96:1/r1.anchor: سورة العلق مكية إجماعا بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم

MAWARDI:96:1/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:1/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
MAWARDI:96:1/r2.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reports that Gabriel first came to the Prophet with a namat, pressed him to read three times, and after the third, forceful pressing, the Prophet answered that he was not a reader before Gabriel recited this verse.
MAWARDI:96:1/r2.anchor: روي عن عبيد بن عمير قال : جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما أتاه بنمط

MAWARDI:96:1/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:1/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:1/r3.claim: The instruction means to begin reciting in the name of the Lord who created.
MAWARDI:96:1/r3.anchor: أي استفتح قراءتك باسم ربك الذي خلق

MAWARDI:96:1/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:1/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:1/r4.claim: The wording distinguishes God as Creator because Quraysh worshipped other gods, none of which created; naming the Creator removes ambiguity.
MAWARDI:96:1/r4.anchor: لأن قريشاً كانت تعبد آلهة ليس فيهم خالق غيره تعالى ،   فميز نفسه بذلك ليزول عنه الالتباس

MAWARDI:96:1/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:1/r5.speaker: عائشة
MAWARDI:96:1/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the order of revelation: this was first, followed by Sūrat Nūn wa-l-Qalam, al-Muddaththir, and al-Ḍuḥā.
MAWARDI:96:1/r5.anchor: روت عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم بعدها

NASAFI:96:1/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:1/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:1/r1.claim: Sūrat al-ʿAlaq is Meccan and consists of nineteen verses.
NASAFI:96:1/r1.anchor: سورة العلق مكية ، وهى تسع عشرة آية

NASAFI:96:1/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:1/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
NASAFI:96:1/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid report that this was the first sūra revealed.
NASAFI:96:1/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد : هى أول سورة نزلت

NASAFI:96:1/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:1/r3.speaker: الجمهور
NASAFI:96:1/r3.claim: The majority hold that al-Fātiḥa was the first revelation, followed by Sūrat al-Qalam.
NASAFI:96:1/r3.anchor: والجمهور على أن الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة القلم

NASAFI:96:1/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:1/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:1/r4.claim: “In the name of your Lord” is in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase: begin with the Lord's name when reading.
NASAFI:96:1/r4.anchor: النصب على الحال . أي : اقرأ مفتتحاً باسم ربك

NASAFI:96:1/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:1/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:1/r5.claim: The sense is, say “In God's name,” then read “the One who created.”
NASAFI:96:1/r5.anchor: كأنه قيل : قل باسم الله ثم اقرأ الذي خلق

NASAFI:96:1/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:1/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:1/r6.claim: The object of “created” is omitted because God alone is the source and creator.
NASAFI:96:1/r6.anchor: لأن المعنى الذي حصل منه الخلق واستأثر به لا خالق سواه

NASAFI:96:1/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:1/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:1/r7.claim: Alternatively, supply “created everything”: the unqualified wording gives no basis to prefer one created thing as the omitted object.
NASAFI:96:1/r7.anchor: أو تقديره خلق كل شيء فيتناول كل مخلوق لأنه مطلق فليس بعض المخلوقات بتقديره أولى من بعض

QURTUBI:96:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:1/r1.claim: The sura is Meccan by consensus, has nineteen verses, and is the first revelation according to most commentators; Gabriel delivered its first five verses at Hira.
QURTUBI:96:1/r1.anchor: وهي مكية بإجماع ، وهي أول ما نزل من القرآن

QURTUBI:96:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI:96:1/r2.claim: Jabir ibn Abdullah says the first revelation was al-Muddaththir, chapter 74.
QURTUBI:96:1/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن أول ما نزل " يا أيها المدثر " [ المدثر : 1 ]

QURTUBI:96:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r3.speaker: أبو ميسرة الهمداني
QURTUBI:96:1/r3.claim: Abu Maysara al-Hamdani says the Opening Sura was the first revelation.
QURTUBI:96:1/r3.anchor: وقيل : فاتحة الكتاب أول ما نزل . قاله أبو ميسرة الهمداني

QURTUBI:96:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI:96:1/r4.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says the first revelation was the command to recite what God prohibited, from 6:151; al-Qurtubi calls the first-sura view correct.
QURTUBI:96:1/r4.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه : أول ما نزل من القرآن

QURTUBI:96:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r5.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI:96:1/r5.claim: Aisha says true dreams were the beginning of revelation, then Gabriel came and delivered the opening verses; al-Bukhari transmits this report.
QURTUBI:96:1/r5.anchor: قالت عائشة : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الرؤيا الصادقة

QURTUBI:96:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r6.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI:96:1/r6.claim: In the two Sahih collections, Aisha recounts true dreams, retreat at Hira, Gabriel's three forceful embraces after Muhammad says he cannot read, and the first five verses.
QURTUBI:96:1/r6.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عنها قالت : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي

QURTUBI:96:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r7.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
QURTUBI:96:1/r7.claim: Abu Raja al-Ataridi recalls Abu Musa teaching this sura in circles at the Basra mosque and saying it was the first sura revealed to Muhammad.
QURTUBI:96:1/r7.anchor: وقال أبو رجاء العطاردي : وكان أبو موسى الأشعري يطوف علينا في هذا المسجد

QURTUBI:96:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r8.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI:96:1/r8.claim: Aisha's reported revelation order after this sura is Nun wa-l-Qalam, al-Muddaththir, then al-Duha; al-Mawardi cites the report.
QURTUBI:96:1/r8.anchor: وروت عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها أول سورة أنزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، ثم بعدها

QURTUBI:96:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r9.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI:96:1/r9.claim: Al-Zuhri says the first revelation extended through ما لم يعلم; Muhammad grieved, Gabriel affirmed he was God's prophet, and after Muhammad asked to be covered and cooled, al-Muddaththir was revealed.
QURTUBI:96:1/r9.anchor: وعن الزهري : أول ما نزل سورة : " اقرأ باسم ربك - إلى قوله - ما لم يعلم "

QURTUBI:96:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:1/r10.claim: Read what has been revealed of the Qur'an, beginning in God's name; al-Qurtubi takes this to mean saying the basmala at the start of each sura.
QURTUBI:96:1/r10.anchor: ومعنى " اقرأ باسم ربك " أي اقرأ ما أنزل إليك من القرآن مفتتحا باسم ربك

QURTUBI:96:1/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:1/r11.claim: The preposition bi in باسم ربك is in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
QURTUBI:96:1/r11.anchor: فمحل الباء من " باسم ربك " النصب على الحال .

QURTUBI:96:1/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:1/r12.claim: Another analysis makes bi mean على; the recited object is omitted, so the sense is to recite the Qur'an and begin it in God's name.
QURTUBI:96:1/r12.anchor: وقيل : الباء بمعنى على ، أي اقرأ على اسم ربك .

QURTUBI:96:1/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r13.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI:96:1/r13.claim: Some say God's name here means the Qur'an and bi is extra, as in 23:20; al-Rai's verse about not reading suras with bi also supports this usage.
QURTUBI:96:1/r13.anchor: وقال قوم : اسم ربك هو القرآن ، فهو يقول : " اقرأ باسم ربك " أي اسم ربك

QURTUBI:96:1/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:1/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:1/r14.claim: Another explanation is simply to remember God's name: Muhammad is commanded to begin recitation by naming God.
QURTUBI:96:1/r14.anchor: وقيل : معنى " اقرأ باسم ربك " أي اذكر اسمه .

RAZI:96:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI:96:1/r1.claim: The commentators say Sūrat al-ʿAlaq was the first revelation.
RAZI:96:1/r1.anchor: زعم المفسرون : أن هذه السورة أول ما نزل من القرآن

RAZI:96:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r2.speaker: آخرون
RAZI:96:1/r2.claim: Others say al-Fātiḥa was revealed first, followed by Sūrat al-ʿAlaq.
RAZI:96:1/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون : الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة العلق

RAZI:96:1/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI:96:1/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats the bāʾ as extra, making the command mean to recite or mention the Lord’s name.

RAZI:96:1/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r4.speaker: الأخطل
RAZI:96:1/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda adduces al-Akhṭal’s line about women who do not recite sūras as evidence for this sense.
RAZI:96:1/r4.anchor: كما قال الأخطل : هن الحرائر لا ربات أخمرة

RAZI:96:1/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r5.claim: Rāzī rejects the analysis: it makes the Prophet’s reply that he cannot read incoherent, commands what he was already constantly doing, and discards the bāʾ without benefit.

RAZI:96:1/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r6.claim: Rāzī prefers reading the command as reciting the Qurʾān, since unqualified recitation is used for it, as in verses about its recitation and gradual revelation.
RAZI:96:1/r6.anchor: القول الثاني : أن المراد من قوله : { اقرأ } أي اقرأ القرآن

RAZI:96:1/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r7.claim: On one analysis, bi-smi rabbika is circumstantial: recite the Qurʾān while beginning with the Lord’s name, saying the basmala first.
RAZI:96:1/r7.anchor: أن يكون محل باسم ربك النصب على الحال

RAZI:96:1/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r8.claim: Rāzī takes this analysis to show that the basmala must be recited at each sūra’s start, rebutting those who do not deem it obligatory.
RAZI:96:1/r8.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه يجب قراءة التسمية في ابتداء كل سورة كما أنزل الله تعالى وأمر به

RAZI:96:1/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r9.claim: Another explanation is to recite the Qurʾān seeking help through God’s name, an instrument for the difficult task like a pen.
RAZI:96:1/r9.anchor: يكون المعنى اقرأ القرآن مستعينا باسم ربك

RAZI:96:1/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r10.claim: A third explanation is to perform the act for God and dedicate it to Him; what is devoted to God is beyond Satan’s interference.
RAZI:96:1/r10.anchor: أي اجعل هذا الفعل لله وافعله لأجله

RAZI:96:1/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r11.claim: Mentioning God before a permissible act can figuratively attribute it to Him and protect it from Satan, who shares food when God’s name is omitted.
RAZI:96:1/r11.anchor: أن ذلك إضافة مجازية كما تضيف ضيعتك

RAZI:96:1/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r12.claim: A permissible act may be dedicated to God when it helps one obey Him, turning it into worship.
RAZI:96:1/r12.anchor: أنه ربما استعان بذلك المباح على التقوى على طاعة الله فيصير المباح طاعة

RAZI:96:1/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r13.claim: Although Allāh is nobler as a name of the divine essence than rabb, worship is urged effectively through God’s active relation as Lord, which makes it incumbent.
RAZI:96:1/r13.anchor: وهو أن الرب من صفات الفعل

RAZI:96:1/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r14.claim: Because this was among the first revelations and the Prophet was frightened, rabb reassures him: the One who raised him will not abandon him; beginning care entails completion.

RAZI:96:1/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r15.claim: Rāzī contrasts God’s adding Himself to the Prophet through lordship with describing the Prophet as His servant in the night journey, and cites a saying that ʿAlī and the Prophet belong to one another.
RAZI:96:1/r15.anchor: تارة يضيف ذاته إليه بالربوبية كما ههنا

RAZI:96:1/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r16.claim: The reciprocal relation is supported by the declaration that obeying the Messenger is obedience to God.
RAZI:96:1/r16.anchor: قوله تعالى : { من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله }

RAZI:96:1/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r17.claim: God says I am yours rather than you are Mine because benefit has so far flowed from Him to the servant; after obedience or repentance He calls the servant His own.
RAZI:96:1/r17.anchor: فيقول الرب تعالى : المنفعة تصل مني إليك

RAZI:96:1/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r18.claim: Once the servant obeys or repents, God adds him to Himself, as in the address to His servants who have wronged themselves.
RAZI:96:1/r18.anchor: أضفتك إلى نفسي فقلت : أنزل على عبده

RAZI:96:1/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:1/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:96:1/r19.claim: The phrase answers how God is the Prophet’s Lord: he and his attributes were once nonexistent and require a creator; bringing him into existence is nurture and establishes God as Lord.
